'''Aiwha''' {{Pronounced|Äē'-wä}}<ref name="NEGAS" /> were flying cetacean creatures that lived on the [[Planet/Legends|planets]] [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] and [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. They could use their wing-fins to either propel themselves through water or to soar through the skies. [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]] were derogatorily referred to as "aiwha-bait" by various clones of [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], bred at a cloning facility on the planet.

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|We've got to stop meeting like this, my friend.|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] to an aiwha after falling on it for a second time|<ref name="ARC Troopers">{{TCW|ARC Troopers (episode)}}</ref>}}
Majestic [[Cetacean/Legends|cetaceans]] that could take to the air,<ref name="DB-aiwha">{{DB|creature|aiwha|aiwha}}</ref> aiwhas could be found in the churning oceans of the planet [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], where they had been domesticated as mounts by the native [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]]. The creatures were strong swimmers, able to launch themselves from the cresting waves and then continue their momentum in flight.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones">{{Film|II}}</ref>

[[File:Aiwhas-ARCT.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Aiwhas swimming beneath the surface of Kamino's oceans]]
Aiwhas and similar creatures could be found on several worlds, including the planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name="DB-aiwha" /> There, they lived in medium-size "[[Pod (social group)|pods]]," feeding on surface-dwelling [[Krill (creature)/Legends|krill]] and the fish (like [[Mee/Legends|daggerts]] and [[Ray/Legends|rays]])<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> found in the huge Naboo lakes. Like other [[Cetacean/Legends|cetaceans]],<ref name="DB-aiwha" /> aiwhas filtered food through the sieve-plates in their baleen. The [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] of Naboo had domesticated aiwhas to accept mounts and provide airborne transportation. Gungans also used the aiwhas as war mounts, using them as reconnaissance and bombers. Aiwhas employed a water-vascular system that allowed them to control their relative density. When they needed to swim underwater, their spongy tissues absorbed water. When flight was required, they expelled this water and shed it to lighten themselves.<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide" />

While some believed the aiwhas on Kamino to have been imported from Naboo, others speculated that this particular breed was entirely the result of [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] technology.<ref name="DB-aiwha" />

Aiwhas were sold by the [[Rothana Heavy Engineering/Legends|Rothana Heavy Engineering]] company to be used as mounts for [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] troops, who used them on worlds that had a breathable atmosphere, and could be used for performing reconnaissance over 5,000 meters overhead, or to traverse between two Imperial outposts without any concern for the trail or terrain. A standard animal cost 45000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] at a starting price, and larger, cargo-hauling breeds were available under the premium pricing model.<ref name="Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Titavian2-woswfg.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Gugans riding aiwhas.]]
The word "aiwha" is a deliberate corruption of "air whale." They are also called Air Whales in the ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]'' game manual.<ref name="Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption Expansion: Prima Official Game Guide">[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption Expansion: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption Expansion'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref>

Aiwhas existed, in one form or another, for over twenty years before being incorporated into a ''Star Wars'' movie. Concept illustrator [[Ralph McQuarrie]] drew flying [[Wikipedia:whale|whales]] to populate [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']], but they were a casualty of budget and effects limitations. They resurfaced as transports on the planet [[Sicemon]] in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']], but were ultimately replaced with the more practical sail barge and skiffs when the world didn't appear in the final film. For [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']], the aiwhas returned as Gungan mounts, but were again dropped from the finished film. For [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']], they were to be possible mounts for the Geonosians before finally finding a home on Kamino.<ref name="DB-aiwha" />

The aiwha bears a striking similarity to the [[Thranta/Legends|thrantas]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], and the [[Neebray/Legends|neebray]] of [[Rugosa/Legends|Rugosa]] and the [[Balmorra Run/Legends|Balmorra Run]], but no [[in-universe]] relation has been documented between any of the three species.

{{Quote|Very vicious, giant, mammalian carnivores, boar-wolves prey on anything that comes across their path.|[[Lyrre T'enna]]'s notes on the boar-wolf.|<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide" />}}
The '''boar-wolves''', or '''borra''', were a predatory animal that lived on the forest moon of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:Boarwolf-howl.png|thumb|left|250px|A howling boar-wolf]]
Boar-wolves had been known to be three meters tall.<ref name="DB-boar-wolf">{{DB|creature|boarwolf|boar-wolf}}</ref> They had hair, sharp teeth, a humped back,<ref name="Caravan of Courage: An Ewok Adventure">''[[Caravan of Courage: An Ewok Adventure]]''</ref> two tusks<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> and large, hooked claws<ref name="Caravan of Courage: An Ewok Adventure" /> that could tear holes in trees. They had pungent and stringy meat.<ref name="The Illustrated Star Wars Universe">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref>

They had a penchant<ref name="The Illustrated Star Wars Universe" /> for howling at the gas giant [[Endor (planet)/Legends|Endor]] when it appeared in the night sky.<ref name="Caravan of Courage: An Ewok Adventure" /> With a keen sense of smell,<ref name="DB-boar-wolf" /> they usually hunted in pairs for prey such as [[Blurrg/Legends|blurrgs]] and [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]], preying anything that came across their path.<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide" /> These truly impressive predators possessed an incredible patience to hide and wait out of sight once they have cornered their prey, having fed on many Ewoks this way.<ref name="The Illustrated Star Wars Universe" />

==History==
Tough the boar-wolves are three times as tall as the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]], they had somehow stumbled upon effective methods for fighting the monsters with spears and poison darts. The Ewoks first baited a clever trap with scraps of bloody meat from other kills and carefully hide a vine net on the forest floor. When a boar-wolf attempted to rip into the fresh meat, the net tangles around its huge armored body, enough to slow and confuse it while the Ewok hunting party charges out of the underbrush. One such kill provided enough meat to feed an Ewok tree village for days, if one could stomach the pungent and stringy meat.<ref name="The Illustrated Star Wars Universe" />

[[File:Gorax-woswfg.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A [[Gorax/Legends|Gorax]] with pet boar-wolves]]
Bear-wolves were sometimes semidomesticated by the primitive [[Gorax/Legends|Gorax]].<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide" /> A Gorax would find a boar-wolf mother who had gone to ground in a cave to give birth to a litter. The Gorax then smashed open the whelping place, killed the mother, and choosed a boar-wolf to take as a pet.<ref name="DB-boar-wolf" /> In keeping with its own fondness for bodily ornamentation, the Gorax would strap leather collars and harnesses on his pup, raising it as a hunting companion.<ref name="The Illustrated Star Wars Universe" />

In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]]<ref name="Star Wars: Behind the Magic">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> one deadly<ref name="DB-Towani, Mace">{{DB|character|macetowani|Towani, Mace}}</ref> domesticated boar-wolf chased [[Cindel Towani|Cindel]] and [[Mace Towani]] through the forest after they left the home of [[Deej Warrick]], trapping them inside the hollow of a tree trunk. In the morning, Deej and his three sons [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket]], [[Widdle Warrick/Legends|Widdle]], and [[Weechee Warrick|Weechee]] went searching for the children and found the boar-wolf lurking in the vicinity. Deej and his two elder sons fought the creature using spears. The boar-wolf was ultimately killed by Wicket, who shot it with a poisoned dart from a blowgun. Upon emerging from their hiding place (from which they witnessed the battle), Mace and Cindel found their [[Jeremitt Towani|father's]] [[Life monitor/Legends|life monitor]] attached to the boar-wolf's collar, put there as an ornament by its owner, a giant Gorax who lived in the [[Forbidden Fortress of the Gorax|Forbidden Fortress]].<ref name="Caravan of Courage: An Ewok Adventure" />

After the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Maldien]] conducted illegal and highly dangerous [[bioengineering]] experiments in a [[Illegal Lab (Corellia)|laboratory]] on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] to create very aggressive and intelligent creatures. This included at least one engineered boar-wolf.<ref name="SWG:CMCOtZ">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=general|Coronet Murmurs: Clear Out the Zoo|Corellia}}</ref>

'''Bordoks''' were a [[species]] of sure-footed [[equine]] [[Diet|herbivores]] [[Homeworld|native]] to the [[Tree|forest]] [[moon]] [[Endor]]. Since the bordoks could carry large loads relative to their small size, the [[Sentience|sentient]] [[Ewok]]s used them as both pack animals and mounts.

==Biology and appearance==
An [[equine]] [[species]],<ref name="BMF 38" /> the bordoks were related to other riding beasts from across [[the galaxy]], including [[pulga]]s, [[fathier]]s, [[orbak]]s, and [[tris]].<ref name="RoS VD">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> They were sure-footed creatures capable of carrying large loads relative to their small size.<ref name="BMF 38" />

==Behavior==
Bordoks were noted for having a friendly behavior, and were domesticable.<ref name="USW" /> They had a [[Diet|herbivorous diet]],<ref name="BMF 38" /> feeding on [[plant]]s.<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

==History==
[[File:Bordok-TheWoklingsTale.png|thumb|Right|180px|A bordok]]
The bordoks [[Homeworld|evolved]] on [[Endor]], a [[Tree|forested]] [[moon]]<ref name="USW" /> that [[orbit]]ted a [[planet]] of the [[Endor (planet)|same name]], in the [[Moddell sector]] of [[the galaxy]]'s [[Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="RoS VD" /> The [[Ewok]]s, a race of diminutive [[Sentience|sentients]] that also originated on Endor, domesticated the bordoks, using them as both pack animals and mounts. Although bordoks were strong for their size, the Ewoks sometimes favored the much larger and stronger [[blurrg]]s, a species of bipedal reptiles, for heavy work.<ref name="BMF 38" />

==Behind the scenes==
A bordok first appeared in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] storybook ''[[Wicket Finds a Way: An Ewok Adventure]]'', which was written by [[Melinda Luke]] and released in [[1984]]. The species was confirmed to be [[canon]] when it received mention in the sourcebook ''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'', released in [[2015]].

'''Brezaks''', also known as '''Zygerrian gliding lizards''', were large [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] [[Diet/Legends|carnivorous]] [[Reptavian/Legends|reptavians]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Zygerria/Legends|Zygerria]]. The [[Zygerrian/Legends|Zygerrian]] [[Slavery/Legends|slavers]] used these as riding mounts to patrol for runaway slaves.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:BrezakFlying-SWE.png|thumb|left|250px|[[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Miraj Scintel/Legends|Miraj Scintel]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] astride a brezak in flight]]
Brezaks had tan undersides with dark brown coloring on their backs. They had horned heads from which their Zygerrian riders could attach reigns to guide the creature from a saddle mount. They possessed strong legs which gave them remarkable speed while running. They also had large flaps of skin which attached to their ribcage that, when retracted, would dangle loosely between their front and hind legs. However, when extended, the brezak could leap into the air and take flight on the wind currents of their Zygerrian homeworld. Their flat tail served as a rudder, and when controlled by a skilled rider, they were quite agile while in flight.

'''Bursas''' were [[Diet/Legends|carnivorous]] quadrupeds native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].

==Characteristics==
Bursas were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]], four-[[Limb/Legends|legged]] [[Diet/Legends|carnivorous]] creatures native to [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. They had tusked snouts and feathery tufts of [[Color/Legends|brown]] [[Hair/Legends|hair]] on their thick-skinned bodies, and were known to build and live in mud huts in the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]].<ref name="TWOSW AFG" /> Prey included [[Mott/Legends|motts]].

==History==
[[File:Bursa.png|thumb|left|250px|Bursas in the swamps of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].]]
Bursas were thought to have predated even the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] race on Naboo. Early Gungans were attacked by the native wild bursas<ref name="TCSWE">{{CSWECite|I|97|bursa}}</ref> while exploring their world. Such behavior was not uncommon in the bursas, who were known to mercilessly destroy Gungan settlements. Bursas led by the warlord [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Rogoe/Legends|Rogoe]] [[Destruction of Otoh Sancture|destroyed]] Boss [[Gallo/Legends|Gallo's]] village, [[Otoh Sancture]],<ref name="SW:GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref> in [[3000 BBY]].<ref name="EA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' places the [[War of the Gungan tribes]] at this time.</ref> However, Gallo's forces healed an injured bursa chief, and a clan of bursas allied with Gallo in the [[Raid on Spearhead|siege]] of Rogoe's Keep.<ref name="SW:GB" />

The [[Amaran/Legends|Amaran]] species took to capturing, breeding, and selling these creatures, which could be trained to dance on their hind legs. At an annual [[Coruscant Livestock Exchange and Exhibition]] held after the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|Destruction of Alderaan]], bursas were displayed at the Exhibition for the first time.<ref name="TWOSW AFG">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:BursaConceptArt.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Concept art from 2000 by Robin Pronovost]]
[[Robin Pronovost]] originally designed the bursas for ''[[The Essential Guide to Episode I]]'', a product that was ultimately never published, at the request of its intended author [[Daniel Wallace]]. The species was to be based on a reference Wallace found in [[George Lucas]]'s notes that the Gungans had once fought against "[[Bear/Legends|bear]]-like creatures."<ref name="DW blog">{{Blog|danwallace|34|Lostwords: The Essential Guide to Episode I}}</ref>

When the ''Essential Guide'' was cut,<ref name="DW blog" /> bursas instead debuted in [[November]] [[2001]]. Their first appearance was in the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'',<ref name="Galactic Battlegrounds">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref> and they were depicted in the reference book ''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]'', which was co-written by [[Terryl Whitlatch]] and [[Bob Carrau]], with the former providing the illustrations.<ref name="TWOSW AFG" />

The '''chrysalide''', also known as the '''chrysalis beast''', was a creature [[Mutant|altered]] by [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]].

==History==
[[File:Chrysalide-FF73.png|thumb|left|180px|A chrysalis rancor]]
It was widely believed that during ancient times, the knowledge of creating the chrysalis beast was formed by the ancient [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. In those early years, the creatures served the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] as pets or protectors to high-ranking officers or powerful [[Noble/Legends|nobles]]. The knowledge for creating such monsters was later encoded within [[Holocron/Legends|holocrons]] and other such tomes, which were buried on Sith [[Planet/Legends|worlds]] such as [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. Many believed that the knowledge of creating such fearsome beasts was lost.<ref name="JATM" />

However, research by [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] uncovered the process of creating chrysalis beasts.<ref name="JATM" /> Using immense alchemical cocoons, he employed this process to transform [[Rancor/Legends|rancors]] into chrysalides<ref name="DSS">''[[The Dark Side Sourcebook]]''</ref> and kept them at the [[Emperor's Citadel|Imperial Citadel]] on [[Byss/Legends|Byss]].<ref name="DE II 5" /> In [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> [[X-1 Viper]] [[Droid/Legends|droids]] controlled by [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Commando/Legends|commandos]] attacked Imperial forces at the Emperor's Citadel and had them all but defeated until the chrysalides were released on the droids. The chrysalides' teeth could chew through Vipers' armor, and the droids proved no match for the chrysalides. They turned the battle in the Empire's favor and caused the surviving New Republic personnel to retreat.<ref name="DE II 5" /> Chrysalides would attack anything in sight apart from other Chrysalides, and would almost always prioritize the largest available target.<ref name="DSS" /> Other creatures mutated into chrysalis beasts were [[Gundark/Legends|gundarks]], [[Katarn/Legends|katarns]], and [[vornskr]]s.<ref name="JATM" />

==Behind the scenes==
The chrysalis beasts were introduced in ''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire II]]''.<ref name="DE II 5" />

You may be looking for the '''[[Drexl-class starfighter|''Drexl''-class starfighter]]''' or '''[[Drexl Roosh]]'''.}} {{Species |image=[[File:Warbeast.jpg]] |name=Drexl |designation=[[Sentience/Legends|Non-sentient]] |class= |subspecies= |races= |height= |length= |wingspan= |mass= |skincolor= |haircolor= |feathers= |eyecolor= |distinctions= |lifespan= |origin=[[Dxun/Legends|Dxun]][[Tales of the Jedi 1|''Tales of the Jedi'' 1]] |habitat=[[Jungle/Legends|Jungle]] |diet=[[Diet/Legends|Carnivorous]] |language= }} {{Quote|What an impressive, flying beast he rides! I've never seen one like it!"
"These beasts originally come from the nearby moon. The Onderonians tame them, but this one was too vicious to be handled.|[[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] and [[Cay Qel-Droma]]|audio=Drexl-DLOTS.flac|[[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith'' audio drama]]}} '''Drexls''', also known as '''warbeasts''', were [[Reptavian/Legends|reptavian]] winged creatures indigenous to [[Dxun/Legends|Dxun]]. ==Overview== [[File:BeastRiders-GAW.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Beast Riders astride their drexl mounts]] These winged lizards possessed heavily muscled bodies covered by purple scales. Their long necks held small heads with short, wide snouts and sharp fangs. An adult drexl's largest teeth were the length of a Human arm, and the creatures had a stature similar to that of a [[Krayt dragon/Legends|krayt dragon]] when fully grown. A fully grown male specimen had a wingspan of twenty meters across. The peculiar orbit of Dxun around [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]] allowed them to migrate to that world. Drexl began life in a [[Larva/Legends|larval]] stage and were born 3 meters tall. They had no wings in this stage, but were extremely fierce as well as vicious. These drexl larvae were more [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] in shape with two legs and two arms, three fingered, clawed hands, a tail, and three rows of spine down their back. The skin of at least some larvae was bright green unlike the dark purple of the adults.''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'' Handling a single Drexl was a difficult task, often requiring three riders to accomplish it. One rider was required to focus their handling on the reins and direct the beast, while another rider was armed with a weapon, with the third rider calling out orders to the controlling rider.''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]'' In many cases, drexls were resistant to the influence of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], however, was able to [[Animal bond|subjugate a drexl's mind]] to his own on a second attempt, shortly after failing due to the unforeseen strength of the reptilian's mind, as compared to a rancor's. ==History== [[File:BeastRidersearly.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Iziz castaways taming the beasts for the first time.]] In early stages of Onderon history, drexls were feared predators that spread terror, attacking the primitive Onderonian villages and forcing the development of the fortified city of [[Iziz/Legends|Iziz]] as the only safe place to live on the planet. The creatures were later trained as mounts by the [[Onderon/Legends|Onderonian]] outcasts, who came to be known as [[Beast Riders]]. Some received names by their riders, such [[Oron Kira|Oron Kira's]] [[Thrasher (drexl)|Thrasher]]. A drexl larva was used in [[General/Legends|General]] [[Vaklu]]'s attempted political coup to take over Onderon. This specimen was used to break down the shield barrier protecting [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Talia (Onderon)|Talia's]] throne room. The larva was later slain by [[Meetra Surik]] and her comrades. Darth Bane was also able to control a drexl when he was trying to get from [[Dxun/Legends|Dxun]] to [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]] after his spaceship crashed. Like the first drexls were able to do, he traveled from Dxun to Onderon on its back, using the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] to keep a [[Protection bubble|bubble of air for them]]. Once he arrived on [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]], his drexl, being much larger than his opponents' (and aided by Bane [[Force power/Legends|using]] the Force to [[Telekinesis/Legends|rip people off their saddle places]] and [[Force lightning/Legends|kill them with bolts of blue fire]]), defeated the beast riders that were harassing [[Darth Zannah/Legends|Darth Zannah]], his apprentice. Frog-dog/Legends.wikitext:
{{Top|ffa}} {{Youmay|the species|[[Frog-dogs|the sports team]]}} {{Species |image=[[File:Bubo.jpg]] |name=Frog-dog |designation=[[Sentience/Legends|Sentient]]{{CSWECite|I|296–297|frog-dog}} |class=[[Reptile/Legends|Reptile]] |subspecies= |races= |height=0.5 [[Meter/Legends|meters]]''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'' |length= |wingspan= |mass=35 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]]''[[Star Wars: Head-to-Head Tag Teams]]'' |skincolor=[[Color/Legends|Brown]],''[[Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal]]'' green, orange-red,[[Star Wars (1998) 8|''Star Wars'' (1998) 8]] purple,{{SeriesRef}} [[Classic Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (comic series)|''Classic Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'']] yellowish dun{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars (Hasbro toy line)|pack=Jabba's Palace Court Denizens|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/sw04ultradenizens.asp}} |haircolor= |feathers= |eyecolor=Purple, red,''[[Super Star Wars: Return of the Jedi]]'' yellow |distinctions=[[Tooth/Legends|Toothy]] maw, independently focusable [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], throaty call{{StoryCite|story=Goatgrass: The Tale of Ree-Yees|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}} |lifespan= |origin= |habitat= |diet=Primarily [[Insect/Legends|insects]] |language=None }} {{Quote|You loathsome two-eyed toad!|Ree-Yees, to Bubo|{{StoryCite|story=Tongue-tied: Bubo's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}}} '''Frog-dogs''' were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Reptile/Legends|lizards]] with both [[Frog/Legends|frog]]-like and [[Dog/Legends|dog]]-like features. Each member of the species had a large cranium that sported two large, protruding [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and long, pointed [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]] that stuck out from the mouth. Two squat [[Limb/Legends|limbs]] with five-fingered hands supported the body, although a frog-dog at rest kept his or her large, bulbous mid-section on the ground as well. The body tapered to a long, thin tail. Frog-dogs caught [[Insect/Legends|insects]] and other prey with a long, sticky tongue that darted from the mouth and retrieved the desired meal. The creatures hopped and waddled from place to place. Frog-dog vocalizations sounded like throaty barks and croaks. Although they were both sentient and highly intelligent, frog-dogs were often mistaken for simple animals. They did nothing to change this misconception and sometimes even used it to their advantage. A frog-dog might deign to live as the pet of another sentient being, for example, trading a life of denigration for a guaranteed source of food. Others worked as [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]] and [[Spy/Legends|spies]], using their unassuming appearance to get into position to complete a particular mission. The frog-dog [[Buboicullaar/Legends|Buboicullaar]] operated in this manner as a "pet" of both a tribe of [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] and of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] in the [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord's]] [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]]. While a member of Jabba's court, Buboicullaar plotted to kill his [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] master. Meanwhile, he foiled a similar assassination scheme by the [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] [[Ree-Yees/Legends|Ree-Yees]]. Upon Jabba's [[Death/Legends|death]] at the [[Great Pit of Carkoon/Legends|Great Pit of Carkoon]], Buboicullaar joined the [[B'omarr Order/Legends|B'omarr Order]]. ==Biology and appearance== {{Quote|Stupid two-eyed maggot fish! It's a good thing I don't need you anymore!|Ree-Yees, to Bubo, as the Gran's assassination plot against Jabba the Hutt progresses|}} [[File:Bubo2_btm.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The frog-dog body included a bulbous head, protruding belly, and long, tapered tail.]] Frog-dogs were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] [[amphibicanoid]]s{{StoryCite|story=Lone Wolf: A Tale of Obi-Wan and Luke|book=SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story}} with features of both [[Frog/Legends|frogs]] and [[Dog/Legends|dogs]].{{CSWECite|I|96|Bubo (Buboicullaar)}} They had two [[Limb/Legends|limbs]] that featured five-fingered hands with craggy [[gray]] nails.{{InsiderCite|60|Who's Who in Jabba's Palace}}''[[Sideshow Collectibles]]'' {{C|Buboicullaar Creature Pack}} Nevertheless, the shortness and splayed arrangement of these appendages kept the frog-dog body low to the ground, making each member of the [[Species/Legends|species]] rest on his or her protuberant belly when at rest. In this position, most frog-dogs stood a mere 0.5 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall, at which height a mass of 35 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] was normal—although at least one specimen on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] grew to at least four times that size. The body tapered to a long, thin tail toward the species' dorsal regions. Rows of bony lumps ran along the back and down the length of the tail. Frog-dogs were covered in warty hides whose pigmentation varied from individual to individual: possible [[Color/Legends|colorations]] included brown, green, orange-red, purple, and yellowish dun, although boils, warts, and mottling of another color could appear as well.''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'' Frog-dog skin hung loosely on the frame; coupled with their large warts, this created folds so deep that small objects could be hidden inside the flaps. A huge cranium dominated the forequarters of a frog-dog's body. Two bulbous, heavy-lidded, frog-like [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' protruded from the top of the visage, their coloration varying from one frog-dog to the next. Possible hues included purple, red, and yellow. Frog-dogs had excellent vision, and they could focus their eyes independently. A wide maw full of row upon row of yellowed, needle-sharp [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]] constituted the species' only other major facial feature. The lower jaw jutted out so as to allow these teeth to protrude even when the mouth was shut.''[[Star Wars Chronicles]]'' The teeth betrayed the frog-dogs' [[Diet/Legends|carnivorous]] diet. Members of the species ate animals of many kinds, although [[Insect/Legends|insects]] formed the main part of their nutrition. A frog-dog fed him- or herself by flicking out the long, prehensile tongue at a target. A sticky fluid allowed the tongue's bulbous tip to adhere to what it touched, so with a quick retraction, a frog-dog's surprised prey could find itself snapped up and in the frog-dog's mouth instantaneously. Frog-dogs in captivity ate nearly anything, including moldy [[Bantha/Legends|bantha]] fat, [[gelatinous chuff]], and pieces of [[Viridian termite]] jaws. Overall, the frog-dogs' appearance made members of other sentient species regard them as simple-minded beasts at best, horrifying monsters at worst. Frog-dogs had two [[Gender/Legends|sexes]], male and female. At least one member of the species carried smaller frog-dogs in the mouth, belching them out when threatened. Frog-dogs were susceptible to [[Cyborrean rabies]], a [[Disease/Legends|disease]] which manifested itself in a pink-colored frothing at the mouth. ==Society and culture== {{Quote|We live within a den of thieves, little one… Why do you want this?''"
"''For the money, of course.|B'omarr monk Evilo Nailati and Buboicullaar, on the frog-dog's decision to kill Jabba|}} [[File:DurosFrogDogAndAurra-SWR08.jpg|thumb|right|275px|Frog-dogs blended into galactic society by playing the role of simple animals.]] In the view of most other sentient species in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], frog-dogs seemed like non-sentient animals. The squat creatures had no native technology or language, and they seemed content to devote most of their time to eating and slobbering on themselves. Some sentient beings even took frog-dogs as pets, feeding them scraps when they begged with plaintive croaking, and keeping them harnessed and leashed with devices that fit around the frog-dog's head and forelimbs.{{StoryCite|story=Skin Deep: The Fat Dancer's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}} In reality, this was just a front. Frog-dogs were highly intelligent beings.''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'', the ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', and ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' all suggest that frog-dogs are highly intelligent, but the ''[[Sideshow Collectibles]]'' "Buboicullaar Creature Pack" calls them only barely intelligent. This article follows the majority of sources. Frog-dogs found it in their best interest to hide their intelligence from others. This afforded them regular access to food—they could eat scraps and crumbs or even something more appealing, like a [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]]—and it enhanced their usefulness as [[Spy/Legends|spies]] and [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]], thus providing them with employment. Frog-dogs understood the value of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] and honored contracts such as [[Bounty/Legends|bounties]] to which they had agreed. Despite their lack of language, frog-dogs communicated their emotions via hisses, whines, croaks of laughter, and a {{Audio|Frog-dogCall.flac|distinctive cry}} that sounded like a cross between a bark and a croak.{{Film|VI}} Their vocalizations could be both loud{{CCG|set=Jabba's Palace Limited|cardname=Bubo}} and throaty.{{DB|character|reeyees|Ree-Yees}} Some members of the species had both a common name, known to outsiders, and a formal name, revealed only to close confidants. Frog-dogs relied heavily on their tongues to interact with the world around them; they tasted people to get a feel for them, as they could tell a great deal about a person by their flavor. The tongue also expressed emotion: curling in disgust, or tickling the roof of the mouth with joy. Frog-dogs at rest often lay with the belly on the ground and the legs splayed, but some also stood upright with the tail held outstretched. They moved by shuffling on their two legs or by hopping. Despite this form of locomotion, frog-dogs could move with great stealth. If threatened, frog-dogs could fight by biting with their sharp teeth and shaking its opponent back and forth. ==History== {{Quote|What's so funny, little one?''"
"''I ate the detonation link, my teacher. The crucial part in Ree-Yees's plan.|B'omarr monk Evilo Nailati and Buboicullaar|}} [[File:BoboOnLeash-RotJAVA.png|thumb|left|250px|The frog-dog Buboicullaar lived as "Bubo," a pet to a tribe of Jawas, even allowing them to keep him on a leash. In reality, Buboicullaar was secretly plotting to kill Jabba the Hutt.]] As early as the period after the signing of the [[Treaty of Coruscant]], frog-dogs were known in the galaxy. At the [[Time/Legends|time]], a [[Huttball/Legends|Huttball]] sports team took its name from the two-legged species. The [[Frog-dogs]] played a game against a rival team, the [[Rotworms]], on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler's]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]].{{TORweb|url=info/media/trailers/huttball|text=Trailer - Huttball}} Frog-dogs at large in the galaxy often found employ as assassins and spies, occupations in which they took advantage of the fact that other sentients often took them for non-sentient beasts. Other members of the species worked as watchbeasts, keeping guard for intruders on their employers' property. Frog-dogs were present in the [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] Tatooine by [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],The events of "[[Lone Wolf: A Tale of Obi-Wan and Luke]]" occur during those of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], which ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]]. frog-dogs were among the species present on Nar Shaddaa. Three rabid members of the species were kept leashed by ''[[go-zeki]]'', [[Gangster/Legends|gangsters]] of the [[Kyuzo/Legends|Kyuzo]] species, and pitted against the fugitive [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], who [[Death/Legends|killed]] all three with his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]. Years later, a frog-dog had joined the court of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]] in his [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]] on the desert world.This frog-dog is visible in ''[[Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal]]''. It is unclear whether this individual is supposed to be Buboicullaar or another member of the species. [[Buboicullaar/Legends|Buboicullaar]], known to the members of Jabba's court as Bubo, lived in the Hutt's palace in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. He was considered the pet of a tribe of Jawas and given the official role of Jabba's personal watchbeast, tasked with alerting the court to anyone entering the throne room. When the [[Droid/Legends|droids]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] arrived in the palace in 4 ABY—and the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] kicked him—Bubo announced their presence by giving a throaty croak. The [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] [[Ree-Yees/Legends|Ree-Yees]] was placed in charge of the frog-dog's feeding and care,{{SWGTCG|set=Galactic Hunters|cardname=Ree-Yees}} which prompted him to use Bubo in an attempt to kill Jabba. The Gran hid a demolitions transmitter among Bubo's flaps of skin.{{CSWECite|III|89|Ree-Yees}} Nevertheless, Bubo hated his keeper, and he ate the device, foiling Ree-Yees's plan. Bubo played up the misconception that he was non-sentient because, in reality, he was a spy and assassin who had been contracted to kill the Hutt; playing dumb allowed him unfettered access to the palace and proximity to his target. During his stay, Bubo befriended the [[B'omarr Order/Legends|B'omarr monks]] who roamed the palace halls in [[B'omarr brain walker|brain walkers]]. The frog-dog studied under the guidance of the monk [[Evilo Nailati]], and the monks were the only inhabitants of the palace to whom Bubo revealed his sentience. After Jabba was killed by the [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] during the [[Battle of the Great Pit of Carkoon]], Bubo gave up his life as an assassin and voluntarily allowed the B'omarr monks to remove his [[Brain/Legends|brain]] from his cranium and place it in a brain walker. In this form, he spent his time pondering philosophy and the universe. ==Behind the scenes== [[File:Bubo_behind_the_scenes.jpg|thumb|right|The frog-dog costume used for ''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'' fit over its performer's torso and head; the puppeteer's legs were hidden under a false floor.]] [[Industrial Light & Magic]] created the frog-dog Bubo as one of the background [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] for Jabba's Palace in the film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], which was first released in [[1983]]. The prototype maquette for the creature had a more upright stance than the final creation, standing on his two legs and not dragging the ground. The final character was a suit worn on the upper half of an actor's body while the performer's legs were hidden in a false floor. In the decades since the film's release, Bubo has often been confused with another creature seen in the film, the [[Worrt/Legends|worrt]]. The two are members of different species. Frog-dogs appear in the [[1994]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Super Star Wars: Return of the Jedi]]'' as enemy characters in levels representing Jabba the Hutt's dance hall and his palace. The game allows the player to take on the role of [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], Leia Organa, or [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] for these stages. The boss enemy of the Jabba's Palace level is a giant frog-dog who spits smaller frog-dogs from its mouth. Because these events conflict with those of the ''Return of the Jedi'' film, this article treats them as non-canonical.This is in keeping with Leland Chee's explanation of canon levels: {{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=488#13131496|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2005-10-25|time=9:28 AM}} [[File:SROTJ_giant_frog-dog.png|thumb|left|thumb|250px|The video game ''Super Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' features a giant frog-dog as the boss enemy for the Jabba's Palace level.]] Author [[Daryl F. Mallett]] expanded on Bubo's backstory in his [[1996]] short story ''[[Tongue-tied: Bubo's Tale]]'', providing his full name—Buboicullaar—and revealing him to be a frog-dog. Mallett was also the first author to establish the species' sentience. Nevertheless, the ''[[Jabba's Palace Limited]]'' expansion of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] treats Bubo as a non-sentient creature rather than an intelligent character. Other sources have followed Mallett's designation. In the story ''[[Goatgrass: The Tale of Ree-Yees]]'', author [[Deborah J. Ross|Deborah Wheeler]] calls the character "a bubo" at one point, although it is unknown if this is a mistake or if "bubo" is a general term for all frog-dogs. Bubo has since appeared in various adaptations of ''Return of the Jedi'', including the [[Return of the Jedi 1|''Marvel'' comics version]] and the [[Star Wars Manga: Return of the Jedi 1|manga adaptation]]. Similarly, frog-dogs have become fixtures of Jabba's court in stories such as ''[[Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal]]'' and ''[[Star Wars Infinities: The Empire Strikes Back]]'', wherein they appear but play '''Gualaar'''<ref name="YouTube">{{SWKidsYouTube|series=Star Wars By the Numbers|text=Every Creature in the Star Wars Movies|video=liYY0_DcgE8|nolive=1}}</ref> were a type of quadruped animal indigenous to the [[mountain]]s and hills of [[Naboo]]. They were tall and broad-barrelled with [[Color|white]] [[Hair|fur]], black [[eye]]s, and a single large horn on their head and two on their snout.<ref name="NoP" /> 

Domesticated a long [[time]] ago by the [[Naboo (people)|Naboo]], the gualaar's build and strength made them perfect beasts of burden. The [[Royal House of Naboo]] kept a herd of gualaar that were used to carry state officials.<ref name="NoP" />

Four gualaar were used to pull the carriage that carried [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]]'s open casket at her [[Padmé Amidala's funeral|funeral]] on the [[planet]] [[Naboo]]<ref name="ROTS" /> in [[19 BBY]].<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], which includes the [[Padmé Amidala's funeral|funeral of Padmé Amidala]], to [[19 BBY]].</ref>

The '''gualaar''' was an [[ungulate]] [[Species/Legends|species]] indigenous to the [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]] and hills of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name="NoP" /> Related to the [[Gualama/Legends|gualama]],<ref name="SWGTNR">{{SWGTCG|set=The Nightsister's Revenge|cardname=Gualaar}}</ref> it was a tall, heavy-bodied beast that possessed horns and [[Color/Legends|white]] [[Hair/Legends|fur]].<ref name="NoP" />

Domesticated a long [[Time/Legends|time]] ago by the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]], the gualaar's build and strength made them perfect beasts of burden. The [[Royal House of Naboo/Legends|Royal House of Naboo]] kept a herd of gualaar that were used to carry state officials.<ref name="NoP" /> They were also trained to pull carriages during [[Funeral/Legends|funerals]] and [[Marriage/Legends|weddings]].<ref name="TCSWE" />

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], shortly after the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> four gualaar pulled the carriage of [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] in the streets of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] during her [[Padmé Amidala's funeral/Legends|funeral procession]].<ref name="Episode III">{{Film|III}}</ref>

'''Gullipuds''' were bulky, loose-skinned, self-inflating amphibians native to the [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. As they were small and easy prey for other animals, like [[Pikobi/Legends|pikobis]], gullipuds would extend their spine to make themselves harder to catch and swallow. When inflated, gullipuds actually bounced. Because of this, they were used in [[Gulliball/Legends|gullipud ball]] games by the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]].

The '''harvester beetle''' was a beetle native to [[Neimoidia/Legends|Neimoidia]], but was settled on all of the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] [[Purse world/Legends|purse worlds]]. They were five [[Meter/Legends|meters]] long, had cutting jaws, three pairs of [[Limb/Legends|legs]], flat heads, and were able to carry up to five times their body weight on their swept backs. Their heads had a pair of looped feelers which served as both feelers and [[Pheromone/Legends|pheromonal]] communicators.

They, along with [[Manax tree/Legends|manax trees]], were an integral source of the [[Fungus/Legends|fungus]] that gave the Neimoidians their riches. The Neimoidians tamed the beetles, which were separated into castes: laborers, harvesters, soldiers, and breeders. At the height of the harvester beetle hierarchy was a queen, who controlled what the other hive members ate.

We don't want to scare 'em.|Ahsoka Tano and Anakin Skywalker encounter a crash of jungle rancors|}} The '''jungle rancor''', also known as the '''hunter rancor''', was a [[subspecies]] of the [[Reptile|reptilian]], [[Sentience|semi-sentient]] [[rancor]] [[species]] [[Homeworld|native]] to the [[planet]] [[Felucia]]. ==Biology and appearance== [[File:Feluciarancor.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A jungle rancor]] An enormous [[subspecies]] of the [[Reptile|reptilian]], [[Sentience|semi-sentient]] [[rancor]] [[species]], jungle rancors, also known as hunter rancors, had clearly defined shells and proportions resembling that of a [[turtle]], with larger heads relative to the rest of their bodies. [[Color|Orange]] and gray spines that ran along their bodies and the sides of their [[tongue]]s. They had brightly colored blue and gray skin, a pair of [[eye]]s with black pupils, brown irises, and yellow sclerae, beaked [[mouth]]s, and webbed [[Limb|hands]] and feet. Their unique physiology imbued them with greater speed and a keener sense of smell than other rancor subspecies. ==Behavior== Vicious, nasty, and more nimble than other beasts of their size, jungle rancors were capable predators preferred to chase down living prey. ==Jungle rancors in the galaxy== [[File:Negotiations.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Blue rancors roamed the colorful jungles of Felucia.]] Though [[Homeworld|native]] to the [[jungle]]s of the [[planet]] [[Felucia]], where they lived in herds{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/bounty-hunters-episode-gallery|text="Bounty Hunters" Episode Gallery}} {{C|Slide 3}} and co-existed in relative harmony with the local [[Felucian]] [[farmer]]s, jungle rancors could also be found on the planet [[Teth]]. In [[21 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' [[Anakin Skywalker]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], and [[Ahsoka Tano]] encountered a herd of jungle rancors on Felucia, which they were careful not to startle. ==Behind the scenes== ===Appearance=== {{Quote|It had a clearly defined shell. The proportions looked more like a turtle, and it had a much bigger head relative to the rest of its body. All these little bumps and stuff give it some scale, so you could believe that this thing was forty feet high.|Kilian Plunkett, on the design of the jungle rancor|}} [[File:Hunter_rancor.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The jungle rancor's original design in ''[[Star Wars: Commander]]'', where it was given the name "hunter rancor," before being updated to give it ''The Clone Wars'' design.]] The jungle rancor was originally developed for the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' feature film]], where it was set to appear in a [[Content cut from Star Wars|scene]] set during the Battle of Teth where a dramatic lightsaber duel between Anakin Skywalker and Asajj Ventress was staged on top of it, though it was ultimately cut from the final film. Despite this, it eventually appeared in "[[Bounty Hunters (episode)|Bounty Hunters]]," the seventeenth episode of the [[canon]] animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''{{'}} [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]], which originally aired on [[April 2]], [[2010]].''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Episode Guide]]'' The jungle rancor began as a cartoon version of the classic rancor from [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], but at [[Dave Filoni]]'s suggestion, lead artist [[Kilian Plunkett]] gave it a horny shell, developing the creature into a new breed resembling [[Wikipedia:Gamera|Gamera]], a [[Wikipedia:Godzilla|Godzilla]]-like [[Wikipedia:Kaiju|Japanese movie monster]]. Plunkett brought in a [[Wikipedia:Sea turtle|sea turtle]] to give [[Tim Brock]], ''The Clone Wars''{{'s}} lead texture artist, ideas for texture, so it would be similar to what you would see in nature. The [[:File:Jungle rancor studies.jpg|design]] had several names before jungle rancor was decided upon, including "snapper rancor," "sea rancor," "swamp rancor," "ranc-turtle," and "turt-ancor." ===Deleted scene=== In the [[Standard year|year]] [[22 BBY]], a jungle rancor was held captive in an abandoned [[B'omarr Order Monastery]] on Teth. During the [[Battle of Teth]], [[Jedi Knight]] Anakin Skywalker and his [[Padawan]] Ahsoka Tano [[Lightsaber duel|dueled]] [[Sith apprentice]] [[Asajj Ventress]] in the monastery's rancor pit. Skywalker ordered Tano to escape with [[Rotta]],[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]] [[Content cut from Star Wars|deleted scenes]] the son of [[Hutt]] [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], who Ventress was attempting to retrieve to convince Jabba to side with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]].[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]] However, as Tano opened a large door on the side of the room on her way out, she accidentally set the jungle rancor loose. Skywalker and Ventress leaped onto the creature's back and continued their duel, and the creature rounded on Tano and the Huttlet. Seeing this, Skywalker slashed at the rancor's back, causing it to violently buck. Tano attacked the rancor, stabbing it in the foot, and the rancor threw the two duelists from its back. The creature rounded on Tano; however, as it leaned toward her, Tano brought up her [[Ahsoka Tano's lightsabers|lightsaber]] and drove the weapon into its [[nose]]. The rancor fell back in pain and sat on Ventress, allowing the [[Jedi]] to escape with the Huttlet. As Ventress ignited one of her [[Asajj Ventress's lightsabers|lightsabers]] into the rancor's rear, the creature reared up and clung to the ceiling, freeing the [[Sith]] apprentice. ==Appearances== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of jungle rancors}} *[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]] {{Del}} *{{TCW|Bounty Hunters (episode)}} {{1st}} *{{VaderImmortal|I}} {{Mo}} *''[[Star Wars: Commander]]'' ==Sources== [[File:Jungle_rancor_concept_art.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Jungle rancor concept art by Kilian Plunkett, here dubbed a "jungle monster"]] *[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Two]] *{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/bounty-hunters-episode-guide|text="Bounty Hunters" Episode Guide | The Clone Wars}} {{1stID|jungle rancor}} *{{SWE|locations|felucia|Felucia}} *{{SW|url=news/monsters-of-the-clone-wars-a-season-two-bestiary-2|text=Monsters of ''The Clone Wars'': A Season Two Bestiary|int=Monsters of The Clone Wars|nolive=1}} *{{SW|url=news/felucia-cellophane-flowers-of-yellow-and-green-and-rancors|text=Felucia: Cellophane Flowers Of Yellow And Green…And Rancors|nolive=1}} *{{BuildFalconCite|21|Guide to the Galaxy}} *{{HelmetCollectionCite|73|Weapons & Uniforms}} *''[[Collapse of the Republic]]'' *''[[Star Wars Bestiary, Vol. 1: Creatures of the Galaxy]]'' *{{Databank|felucia|Felucia}} *{{Databank|rancor|Rancor}} ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |es=Rancor de la jungla |fr=Rancor de la jungle |ja=ジャングル・ランコア }} [[Category:Creatures of Felucia]] [[Category:Jungle and forest creatures]] [[Category:Rancor subspecies]]

'''Jungle rancor''' was the name given to one of a number of [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]] [[Subspecies/Legends|subspecies]] bred by animal dealers.

==Characteristics==
[[File:Feluciarancor.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A jungle rancor]]
Notable distinctions from the common rancor were its brightly [[Color/Legends|colored]] skin, sharp spines that ran along much of its body as well as its tongue, and webbing between its fingers and toes.<ref name="TCWVG" /> The jungle rancor also had much larger jaws than the common rancor.

==History==
One of these creatures was used by a crime syndicate on [[Teth/Legends|Teth]] to dispose of its enemies.<ref name="TCWVG" />

[[File:Jungle_rancors.png|thumb|right|280px|Jungle rancors on Felucia]]
Early in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], a jungle rancor was found in the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]] temple. A pair of Jedi assigned to [[Mission to Dathomir (Clone Wars)|investigate]] the temple were chased by the beast, but they were able to lead it into a pit, trapping it.<ref name="Jedi A'liances">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Jedi Alliance]]''</ref>

Jungle rancors were also found on the jungle [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]]. After crash-landing on the planet, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] crossed paths with two of the large beasts. Strangely, nearby villagers did not seem to be threatened by these rancors.<ref name="BH" />

'''Kaadu''' were large, flightless [[Reptavian/Legends|reptavians]] that inhabited the [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planets]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] and [[Obredaan]] as well as the moon of [[Rori/Legends|Rori]]. [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] frequently used them as mounts.

==Characteristics==
[[File:Kaadu-wosfg.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Male and female with young]]
The kaadu was a two-legged reptavian at home both on land and in the [[Water/Legends|water]]: they were excellent runners and strong swimmers, as their lung capacity allowed them to remain underwater for up to two [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]].<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> Kaadu came in shades of [[Color/Legends|yellow]] and bright oranges. The area around their [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] was a periwinkle color.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace" />

Kaadu had sharp hearing and a keen sense of smell.<ref name="DB-kaadu" /> They lacked upper incisors, and as such were unable to chew their food. Their diet consisted primarily of [[Snail/Legends|snails]], [[tlickweed]], and standard aquatic plants. Their blunt, hoof-like claws provided surefootedness. The stub tail counterbalanced the head.<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide" />

They could be found in huge, sexually segregated flocks (20–100 individuals on average), with the total record documented as 3.4 million individuals. Male flocks and female flocks came together during mating, at which time the males became more colorful with yellows and purples. They often had close familial ties. Kaadu females laid their eggs on land, often in fields, but also on riverbanks, where they made elevated mud nests that they lined with vegetable matter. Because predators such as the [[Peko-peko/Legends|peko-peko]] ate unattended kaadu eggs, the average clutch of eggs was usually 10 to 12 at a time. Six to eight in a clutch would usually make it to hatching. The young were fully precocial at hatching.<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide" />

Predators of the adults included [[Narglatch/Legends|narglatches]] and [[Zalaaca/Legends|zalaacas]].<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide" />

Kaadu meat was comestible. The cookbook ''[[Essential Cooking Skills]]'' detailed how to best cook that meat.<ref name="SWG:ECS">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=item|ESSENTIAL COOKING SKILLS}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:Kaadu_Cavalry_SECR.jpg|thumb|right|180px|A Gungan of the Kaadu Cavalry on his kaadu mount]]
The [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] long ago domesticated the kaadu.<ref name="DB-kaadu" /> Kaadu were known to be fearless, and many were domesticated by Gungan warriors as steeds during times of conflict, or as patrol animals to police the Gungan [[City/Legends|cities]]. Kaadu were highly loyal to their owners; it was said that a Gungan and his kaadu made an inseparable team. Warriors often decorated their steeds with huge [[titavian]] feathers.<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide" /> [[Officer/Legends|Officers]] of the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]] rode into [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|battle]] against the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] upon their kaadu mounts.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace">{{Film|I}}</ref>

They were also encountered by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] during their [[Second mission to Obredaan|task]] of finding missing [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]] and [[Eeth Koth/Legends|Eeth Koth]] in the swamps of [[Obredaan]].<ref name="Star Wars: Obi-Wan video game">[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The kaadu was originally developed as a beast of burden on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] for [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']]. The creature was later given more aquatic characteristics and transferred to Naboo. The kaadu seen in Episode I are computer-generated models. They run with a hopping trot that moves them briskly across the battlefield.<ref name="DB-kaadu">{{DB|creature|kaadu|kaadu}}</ref>

''[[Episode I Adventures 15: The Final Battle]]'' erroneously describes the kaadu as a four-legged creature.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 15: The Final Battle">''[[Episode I Adventures 15: The Final Battle]]''</ref>

The sound for the kaadu was created from the slowed-down sound of pigs and the sound of the blowhole of a whale.<ref name="Drawing from the Present: Familiar Creatures in a Galaxy Far, Far Away">{{SW|url=news/drawing-from-the-present-familiar-creatures-in-a-galaxy-far-far-away|text=Drawing from the Present: Familiar Creatures in a Galaxy Far, Far Away|int=Back from the Drawing Board|nolive=1}}</ref>

A '''katarn''' was a predatory quadruped [[Reptomammal/Legends|reptomammal]] native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]].

==Overview==
[[File:Dragontroopercw.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[dragon trooper]] on his katarn.]]
Katarns had slender bodies with [[Rodent/Legends|rodent]]-like tails, and narrow faces leading back to a cartilaginous ridge protecting their neck and shoulders. Their paws had opposable digits, and their lower [[Limb/Legends|limbs]] were covered with sharp spurs, both of which allowed them to climb and hang from the branches of the giant [[Wroshyr tree/Legends|wroshyr trees]] and feed on [[Tree-burrower/Legends|tree-burrowers]].

Katarns were creatures of great importance in the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]]' culture. The Wookiees, who called the katarn the "Old Prince", hunted them in their [[Hrrtayyk ceremony/Legends|hrrtayyk ceremony]]. Wookiees said the katarns were born by a wound to Kashyyyk that fell from the sky ages ago and made a home for the katarn. The katarns then hunted the Wookiees, thus unlocking the Wookiees' "inner fire". To thank the katarn, the Wookiees hunted them. They believed that someday it would be the katarn's turn to hunt the Wookiees again.

Katarns were ferocious and merciless predators which would track their prey for long periods before choosing an opportune moment to strike. They had been described as "silent, shadowy, and deadly," qualities which made them the mascot of [[Judder Page/Legends|Judder Page's]] [[Katarn Commandos]].

Some katarns were domesticated as the war-mounts of Wookiee [[dragon trooper]]s. On another note, there was a small subspecies of katarn that populated the [[Shadowlands/Legends|Shadowlands]]. These katarns had no climbing abilities, as evidenced by their four large trunk-like legs. They also had two small dangling manipulator arms. They had more rounded out edges than the main katarn species and two large tusks. The reformed [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] battled several of these in his second trip to find the Kashyyyk star map.

The '''Kwazel Maw''' was a large aquatic predator that was [[Homeworld|native]] to the [[swamp]]s of the [[planet]] [[Rodia]]. During the [[Clone Wars]], the [[Gungan]] [[Jar Jar Binks]] encountered one of these creatures while on a [[mission to Rodia]], which he befriended and named "[[Bogey (Kwazel Maw)|Bogey]]." Bogey helped Binks secure the [[Trade Federation]] [[Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray]]'s capture by toppling his [[Sheathipede-class transport shuttle|shuttle]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:Kwazel_Maw.png|thumb|left|275px|A Kwazel Maw in its swamp habitat]]
Kwazel Maw were giant aquatic [[Slug (creature)|slugs]]<ref name="BJ Episode Gallery">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/bombad-jedi-episode-gallery|text="Bombad Jedi" Episode Gallery}}</ref> who lurked at the bottom of the [[swamp]]s of [[Rodia]]. Their skin served as a major distinctive feature, highlighted by glowing [[Bioluminescence|bioluminescent]] markings and offering enough resistance to deflect [[blaster]] bolts and even some [[missile]]s.<ref name="TVE" />

The large creatures had cavernous mouths which it used to roar. When opened, it would allow them to consume larger prey, even the size of a [[humanoid]], whole. Their [[Color|yellow]] [[eye]]s had eyelids that would close when sleeping underwater. They had multiple appendages at the front and back of their body and a large tail.<ref name="TVE" />

Despite naturally inhabiting swamps, it appeared Kwazel Maw were equally comfortable on land.<ref name="Bombad Jedi" />

==History==
{{Quote|There's a bad boogie-monster down dere, you betcha.|Jar Jar Binks after coming face-to-face with a Kwazel Maw|<ref name="Bombad Jedi" />}}
During a [[Galactic Republic|Republic]] mission to the [[planet]] [[Rodia]], [[Jar Jar Binks]] discovered and eventually befriended a Kwazel Maw.<ref name="Bombad Jedi" />

Binks travelled to the planet with [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] and [[C-3PO]] to discuss the continuation of Rodia's allegiance to the Republic with [[Senator]] [[Onaconda Farr]]. Unbeknownst to the trio, they were being led into a trap devised by [[Trade Federation]] [[Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray]] to capture Amidala. After Binks learned of Amidala's arrest, he rushed to her rescue, donning a [[Jedi]] [[Jedi apparel|robe]] that he had found aboard her [[H-type Nubian yacht|ship]]. He was soon discovered by Gunray and his accompanying [[B1-series battle droid|battle droids]], however, and escaped underwater via a grate.<ref name="Bombad Jedi" />

[[File:Good_boy_Boogie.png|thumb|right|275px|Binks and "Bogey" together]]
There, Binks discovered a Kwazel Maw, and only just managed to escape the beast. Later, however, Binks found himself underwater once more, this time evading a [[missile]] that had been fired by a [[B2-HA super battle droid]]. In the process, Binks came face-to-face again with the Kwazel Maw, and was swallowed whole by the creature, only for it to shrug off the missile and then release the [[Gungan]]. With the beast seemingly friendly towards him, Binks affectionately stroked its hide and dubbed it "[[Bogey (Kwazel Maw)|Bogey]]."<ref name="Bombad Jedi" />

Later, as Amidala and C-3PO were set to be executed by Gunray, Binks distracted the [[Droideka|droid executioners]] and was then assisted by Bogey, who launched out from underwater and destroyed a number of battle droids, with Binks on its back. As Gunray looked to flee amid the confusion, Bogey toppled his [[Sheathipede-class transport shuttle|shuttle]],<ref name="Bombad Jedi" /> the ''[[Lapiz Cutter]],''<ref name="BMF 54">{{BuildFalconCite|54|Starship Fact File}}</ref> off the edge of the [[hangar]], cutting off his escape route. Gunray was then arrested by Amidala and Farr, while Binks was commended for his bravery, with Bogey looking on.<ref name="Bombad Jedi" />

==Behind the scenes==
The design of the Kwazel Maw was based off an unused [[Ralph McQuarrie]] design, which was originally for a swamp slug creature on [[Dagobah]].<ref name="BJ Trivia Gallery">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/bombad-jedi-trivia-gallery|text="Bombad Jedi" Trivia Gallery}}</ref>

{{Top}} {{Species |image=[[File:KwazelMaw-TCWVG.png]] |name=Kwazel Maw |designation=[[Sentience/Legends|Non-sentient]] |class= |subspecies= |races= |height= |length=88 [[Meter/Legends|meters]]''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]'' |wingspan= |mass= |skincolor= |haircolor= |feathers= |eyecolor= |distinctions=Bioluminescent markings |lifespan= |origin=[[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]] |habitat=[[Ocean/Legends|Sea]] |diet=[[Diet/Legends|Carnivore]] |language= }} {{Quote|There's a bad boogie-monster down dere, you betcha.|[[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]]|{{TCW|Bombad Jedi}}}} The '''Kwazel Maw''' was a large predator native to the oceans of [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]]. ==Characteristics== [[File:Kwazel_Maw.png|thumb|left|200px|"Bogey", a Kwazel Maw in the swamps of Rodia.]] They were clumsy swimmers and preferred to cling to undersea canyon walls, using their antennae to sense for prey that wandered too close. They could live up to 100 [[Standard year/Legends|years]].''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: The Visual Guide]]'' Kwazel Maws were very similar in appearance to the [[Swamp slug/Legends|swamp slugs]] of [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]]''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]'' save for the bio-luminescent markings along their bodies, a fin at the end of the tail, and their much greater size. Their skin was impervious to most laser blasts. ==History== {{Quote|I ''knew'' there was something in the water."
"Maybe its bark is worse than its bite."
"I hope you're right, for ''both'' our sakes!|[[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], upon encountering a Kwazel Maw|''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Jedi Alliance]]''}} While on a [[Mission to Rodia/Legends|mission on Rodia]], [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]] encountered a friendly Kwazel Maw, whom he affectionately named "[[Bogey (Kwazel Maw)/Legends|Bogey]]." This particular specimen seemed to be easily domesticated by Jar Jar, and also allowed [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] to approach it. Bogey came in handy during the battle, allowing Jar Jar to stand on its back while it destroyed all the droids in its path, unharmed by their lasers due to its thick hide. It also toppled [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray's]] shuttle into the sea, allowing the Viceroy to be captured by the Republic forces. Later that [[22 BBY/Legends|year]] the bounty hunter [[Robonino/Legends|Robonino]] was swallowed by a Kwazel Maw during a fight with [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]] on [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]]. He was later regurgitated by the Kwazel Maw, where he was promptly captured by the waiting Fisto and his troops.[[The Clone Wars: Hunting the Hunters (Part II)|''The Clone Wars: Hunting the Hunters'' (Part II)]] ==Behind the scenes== [[File:SwampSlug-McQuarrie.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Ralph McQuarrie's concept art, on which the Kwazel Maw is based.]] The Kwazel Maw design is based on [[Ralph McQuarrie]]'s design for the swamp slug creatures of [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]].{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode008.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Bombad Jedi}} ==Appearances== *''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Jedi Alliance]]'' *{{TCW|Bombad Jedi}} {{1st}} *''[[The Clone Wars: Bombad Jedi]]'' *{{TCW|Cloak of Darkness}} {{Flash}} *[[The Clone Wars: Hunting the Hunters (Part II)|''The Clone Wars: Hunting the Hunters'' (Part II)]] ==Sources== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Kwazel Maws}} *''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: The Visual Guide]]'' {{1stm}} *{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode008.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Bombad Jedi}} *''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' *''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' *[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season One|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season One]] *''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]'' *{{InsiderCite|131|We Need to Talk About Jar Jar|reprint=1}} *[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.32|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Comic 6.32]] *''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide: Updated and Expanded]]'' *''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Episode Guide]]'' ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |de=Kwazelschlund |nl=Kwazel Maw |pl=Kwazel maw/Legendy |pt=Kwazel Maw }} [[Category:Aquatic creatures]] [[Category:Blaster-resistant creatures]] [[Category:Creatures of Rodia]] [[Category:Creatures of unspecified biology]] [[Category:Non-sentient species]] [[Category:Predatory creatures]]

The '''leaf-tail''' was a [[species]] of [[Sentience|non-sentient]] winged [[rodent]] found on the [[planet]] [[Dagobah]]. Leaf-tails were about thirty [[centimeter]]s in length with a wingspan of roughly the same width. They possessed a membrane on the end of their tail that resembled the [[Plant|leaf]] of a [[gnarltree]], giving the leaf-tail its name and allowing the rodents to camouflage themselves and avoid predators.<ref name="NoP" />

Leaf-tails were flying [[Diet|omnivores]], and although they preferred [[Berry|berries]], they could sustain themselves on [[insect]]s and other smaller rodents. Individual leaf-tails posed no threat to sentients, but should an individual come across a leaf-tail nest, dozens of the rodents could attack in a swarm using their [[Tooth|teeth]]. During the [[Galactic Civil War]], the tiny handful of [[smuggler]]s who occasionally traveled to Dagobah in order to capture [[jubba bird]]s told tales of leaf-tails causing near catastrophic damage to [[starship]]s by chewing through cabling.<ref name="NoP" />

==Behind the scenes==
In the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], leaf-tails were mentioned in ''[[Nexus of Power]]'', a [[2016]] supplement to the ''[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny]]'' roleplaying game made by [[Fantasy Flight Games]].<ref name="NoP" /> The [[Leaf-tail/Legends|species]] originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was first mentioned in the [[2001]] reference book ''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]'', which was written by [[Terryl Whitlatch]] and [[Bob Carrau]] with illustrations by Whitlatch.<ref name="Wildlife">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref>

'''Leaf-tails''' were a small [[Rodent/Legends|rodent]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]].

==Description==
A non-sentient species of winged rodent, leaf-tails had membranous leaf-like tails that aided in balance and camouflage. Omnivorous, leaf-tails ate both berries and rodents to sustain itself. They had expandable cheeks used to gather food—typically [[Cyanoberry/Legends|cyanoberries]]. They had great agility which helped them jump from tree to tree. Living in nests, leaf-wings attacked in swarms of dozens.<ref name="NoP" /> The rodents were the main prey of creatures such as [[Bogwing/Legends|greater bogwings]].
