Loth-wolves had a special connection to [[the Force]] and Lothal, where they acted as the guardians of the [[Light side of the Force|light side]] on the world. By the [[time]] of the [[Imperial Era]], Loth-wolves were widely believed to be extinct, yet in [[1 BBY]], members of the [[Spectres]] rebel cell encountered Loth-wolves while undertaking an [[Theft of the TIE Defender Elite|undercover mission]] on the planet for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]]. ==Biology and appearance== {{Quote|Ezra, how did you know the wolves could do that?''"
"''I didn't.|Zeb and Ezra after experiencing hyperspace tunneling|}} [[File:Loth-wolf_pack_WaaD.png|thumb|left|250px|A pack of Loth-wolves.]] Loth-wolves were a canine [[species]] native to the planet Lothal. They came in a variety of [[color]]s including white, black, and silver. Loth-wolves were [[Sentience|sentient]], and also capable of speaking [[Galactic Basic Standard]], although they did not speak often. They were strongly connected to [[the Force]] of Lothal, making them capable of remarkable feats, including [[hyperspace tunneling]] and crossing through the [[World Between Worlds]]. Loth-wolves were large creatures, taller than a [[human]]. One individual, [[Dume]], was abnormally large even by the standards of Loth-wolves.{{Databank|dume|Dume}} ==History== ===Early history=== {{Quote|Loth-cat, loth-cat, Loth-wolf run. Pick a path and all is done.|Ezra Bridger using the Lothalite children's rhyme while trying to decide which way to go in the Lothal Jedi Temple in [[4 BBY]]|{{Rebels|Path of the Jedi}}{{RebelsDate|110}}}} Loth-wolves were a concern for many of Lothal's early settlers, and [[farmer]]s were known to carry [[blaster]]s to protect themselves from creatures.''[[Servants of the Empire: Edge of the Galaxy]]'' They were depicted in [[cave]] [[painting]]s made by the ancient people of the planet, and were named in a [[Lothalite]] children's rhyme.''[[Ezra's Duel with Danger]]'' By the [[Imperial Era]], Loth-wolves were widely thought to be extinct as they had not been seen [[101 BBY|for one hundred years]]. During the [[Clone Wars]], [[Anakin Skywalker]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], and [[Ahsoka Tano]] passed by a [[Mission to Mortis|depiction]] of a Loth-wolf while on [[Mortis]].{{TCW|Overlords}} ===Reign of the Empire=== ====Crossing paths==== {{Quote|I... I thought I saw something. I think it's a Loth-wolf. No one's seen them in 100 years, but I think I keep seeing one today.
A Loth-wolf? Like from those old cave paintings?|Ezra and Sabine, as Ezra saw it the first time|}} In [[1 BBY]],{{RebelsDate|406}} Thus, the last reported sighting of a Loth-wolf must have happened by circa [[101 BBY]]. [[Ezra Bridger]] encountered one on a scouting [[Theft of the TIE Defender Elite|mission]] in the fields of Lothal. Having a special connection to the Force, they could sense that Lothal was in danger from the [[Galactic Empire]], an organization of the [[Dark side of the Force|dark side]]. The wolf later assisted Bridger and [[Sabine Wren]] in escaping from Imperial forces. It put Wren to [[sleep]] merely by saying the word and vanished when the other [[Spectres]] were near. [[File:White_Loth-wolf_wbw_K.png|thumb|right|250px|Loth-wolves could travel through the World Between Worlds.]] Later, the [[White Loth-wolf|white wolf]], along with two other wolves, transported Bridger, Wren, [[Garazeb Orrelios|Zeb Orrelios]], [[Kanan Jarrus]], and [[Ryder Azadi]] from a [[Loth-wolf den|wolf den]] in the northern hemisphere to a [[Lothal cliff dwelling|cliff dwelling]] in the southern hemisphere, using a [[Hyperspace tunneling|means]] reminiscent of [[hyperspace]] travel and were able to enter the [[World Between Worlds]],{{Rebels|A World Between Worlds}} as indicated by their ability to walk through space. The wolf took a strong interest in Kanan Jarrus, whom he referred to by his [[Reproduction|birth]] name, "Dume." The white wolf, along with the two black wolves, stopped Jarrus from returning to [[Capital City|Lothal City]] to rescue [[Hera Syndulla]], and gave him a message.{{Rebels|Rebel Assault}} While Kanan meditated before going on his fateful [[Rescue of Hera Syndulla (Lothal)|mission to rescue her]], it silently watched him through the grass.{{Rebels|Jedi Night}} ====Spirit guides==== [[File:White_Loth-wolf_Ezra_DUME.png|thumb|left|250px|Dume counsels Ezra Bridger after the death of his master.]] After Kanan's death at the hands of [[Governor]] [[Arihnda Pryce|Pryce]], Ezra, while mourning, was ambushed by the white wolf and the two others, who pursued him until nightfall. Ezra, now lost, sat by a large mound and fell asleep. He then woke up to find the three wolves staring at him, and behind him an even larger wolf named "[[Dume]]." After a conversation with Dume, the wolves gave Ezra a [[Lothal Key Stone|stone]] from the Lothal Jedi Temple. Following this, Ezra managed to reunite with the other [[Spectres]] and told them about the plan to get to the temple. The Loth-wolves appeared out of the grass, and the crew rode them to the temple as the wolves once again used a hyperspace travel-like means to reach it. Afterwards, Ezra used the stone given to him as a key to unlock the [[Painting of the Mortis gods|mural of the Mortis gods]] on the temple's wall. Once he did so, painted Loth-wolves flanking the mural suddenly came to life and started howling and walking to the right. The painted wolves then ran in a circle, forming a portal to the World Between Worlds.{{Rebels|Wolves and a Door}} Inside the World Between Worlds, Ezra passed by a constellation-like depiction of a Loth-wolf in the sky. After Ezra returned from the world and closed the temple, the painted wolves stopped forming the portal and ran towards the portrait of the [[Father (Mortis)|Father]] as the temple collapsed. After this incident, Ezra finally came to terms with Kanan's death; as he did so, he saw the white wolf in the distance, which looked at him and then departed. ====Liberation of Lothal==== {{Quote|Hey, Wolffe. Can you believe it?''"
"''What?''"
"''The wolves! You got your Wolfpack back!''"
"''Yeah. They fight just like the boys.|Gregor and Wolffe during the Battle for Lothal|audio=WolfPackBack-AFH.flac|{{Rebels|A Fool's Hope}}}} [[File:Loth-wolf_chew_toy_AFH.png|thumb|right|250px|A pair of Loth-wolves grab hold of a stormtrooper.]] Several Loth-wolves aided Ezra in capturing Pryce by luring [[Rukh]] and several stormtroopers into the cave. The wolves' ferocity easily overpowered the Imperial soldiers. Pryce was captured by the white Loth-wolf, who had tossed Rukh off the base. The [[clone trooper]]s [[Wolffe]] and [[Gregor]] commenting on how they fought "like the boys" back in the Clone Wars, referring to the [[104th Battalion]] "Wolfpack" that Wolffe had commanded. Killing most of the stormtroopers, the wolves focused on the surviving stormtroopers, who were intimidated and quickly surrendered to the rebels. Rukh, who survived the fall, overpowered Wolffe, [[Mart Mattin]], and [[Cikatro Vizago]] and prepared to kill them. However, the white-Loth wolf appeared, and Rukh barely managed to escape it by boarding a TIE gunfighter. The Loth-wolf growled as Rukh fled the scene, though it stayed to ensure the three rebels' safety before leaving. This allowed the three rebels to assist Ezra's plan to [[Liberation of Lothal|liberate]] Lothal by summoning a pod of [[purrgil]] to attack [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn's]] [[Seventh Fleet (Galactic Empire)|blockade]] above Lothal.{{Rebels|Family Reunion – and Farewell}} ===Post-Empire=== With the Imperial presence gone on Lothal, several Loth-wolves could be seen running in the open plains. Wren later drew two Loth-wolves as part of a [[Spectres mural|mural]] of her rebels which was [[Spectres mural ceremony|unveiled]] in Capital City for the tenth anniversary of Lothal's liberation.{{Ahsoka|Part One: Master and Apprentice}} She also drew a sketch of a Loth-wolf head on the walls of her home in the [[LothalNet comm tower E-272]].{{SW|url=news/inside-ahsoka-easter-eggs-sabine-wren|text=Inside ''Ahsoka'': 12 Easter Eggs from Sabine Wren's Lothal Lookout}} ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|Well, to know Dave Filoni is to know about his love of wolves. Yeah, yeah, big fan. So, I think it was really nice that we can like end our story and incorporate the ideas of wolves and having a supernatural element to them. And I think the first we found out, you showed us the sketch of them and they looked so cool, and it, you know they're a bit eeiri, they're a little bit scary, they're regal, they're like all, all these things. And also, we just know you, we know each other pretty well at this point, and so I, I was just happy that Dave got some wolves on our show below the end sort of thing.|Sabine Wren voice actor [[Tiya Sircar]] during the Q&A on the Walt Disney Studios Lot on [[March 2]], [[2018]]|{{YouTube|video=guv0tGVOdN8|text=Star Wars Rebels Season 4 Series Finale Q & A with Dave Filoni & Cast|channel=SkywalkingThroughNeverland|name=Skywalking Through Neverland|date=2018-03-06}}}} The Loth-wolfs first appeared in the episode "[[Flight of the Defender]]" from the [[Star Wars Rebels Season Four|fourth and final season]] of the animated series ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' in [[2017]] after having previously been mentioned in the series' [[Star Wars Rebels Season One|first season]] and the ''[[Star Wars Rebels: Servants of the Empire]]'' novels. ===Origins and development=== They were based on a sketch from the sketchbook of series creator [[Dave Filoni]].''[[The Art of Star Wars Rebels]]'' During the development of his previous animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' Filoni,{{SWYouTube|lS4sclln5J4|Ahsoka's Untold Tales Panel | Star Wars Celebration Europe 2016}} who is a huge fan of wolves ever since seeing the film [[Wikipedia:Never Cry Wolf (film)|''Never Cry Wolf'']] as a young child, would sometimes draw the character [[Ahsoka Tano]] and other characters{{WebCite|url=http://www.comicon.com/2017/10/31/dave-filoni-on-his-fascination-with-wolves-and-star-wars-rebels-return-to-lothal|text=Dave Filoni On His Fascination With Wolves And Star Wars Rebels’ Return To Lothal |author=Erik Amaya|date=2017-10-31|archivedate=20200425031947}} riding wolves because he liked it and Ahsoka had been inspired by the character San in the [[1997]] anime film ''[[Wikipedia:Princess Mononoke|Princess Mononoke]]''—Filoni's favorite film{{WebCite|url=https://nerdist.com/star-wars-rebels-princess-mononoke-Loth-wolf|text=Star Wars Rebels: What is the Loth-Wolf?|author=Ratcliffe, Amy|date=2017-10-31|archivedate=20180123121836}} {{C|Updated on [[January 19]], [[2018]]}}—who also rode a large wolf. However, ''[[Star Wars]]'' and ''The Clone Wars'' creator [[George Lucas]] never cared for the concept{{WebCite|url=http://www.mania.com/star-wars-celebration-europe-ii-clone-wars-update_article_138065.html|text=Star Wars Celebration Europe II: Clone Wars Update|author=Robert T. Trate|date=2013-07-27|archivedate=20130809073132|nolive=1}} and teased him about it. During the development of the series' final arc of the [[Siege of Mandalore]] and [[Order 66]], Filoni conceived the idea that Ahsoka would have been chased by her clone troopers into a "forest" of the legs of giant wolves and they would have defended Ahsoka against the troopers and let her ride away on them. However, Filoni discarded the idea because he felt that it would be too self serving. ''Star Wars Rebels'' was code named "WOLF" during production as a nod to Filoni's well known love and obsession for the animals.{{SW|url=news/10-things-you-did-not-know-about-star-wars-rebels|text=10 Things You Didn't Know About ''Star Wars Rebels''}} When Filoni announced that wolves would appear in ''Rebels'', the development team saw it as a "huge deal" they wanted to get right because of it. The animators were also nervous due to the difficulty of depicting the animals as realistic, while also fitting with the series' art style, and the challenges of correctly animating their fur.{{RebelsRecon|Zxz8sga3XLM|#4.3: Inside "The Occupation" & "Flight of the Defender" | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/disneyxd-rebels-recon-inside-the-occupation-and-flight-of-the-defender}} The Loth-wolves' design was refined by [[JP Balmet]], and Balmet also created their animation model, which was finished on [[July 15]], [[2016]]. The model for the grey-furred version was adapted from Balmet's white version by [[Chris Voy]] and finished on the same day,{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/flight-of-the-defender-episode-guide|text="Flight of the Defender" Episode Guide | Star Wars Rebels}} and the black version was designed by [[DJ Welch]]. The models' fur required 416 different control points for the individual hair tufts to move correctly. The rock art of the Loth-wolves in the Lothal Jedi Temple and the cave paintings was designed by [[Andre Kirk]] and the wolves in Sabine Wren's mural were designed by [[Kilian Plunkett]]. In an interview at a [[Wikipedia:FanExpo Canada|FanExpo Canada]] panel in September 2017, ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' creator [[Dave Filoni]] compared the Loth-wolf with the [[Bendu]], neither good nor bad in terms of the Force. He included the wolf because of his love of the creature, but also because of the cultural perception of wolves as guides. He further stated that the Loth-wolf is a natural element of the Force on Lothal. Filoni later confirmed that the Loth-wolves depiction had been heavily inspired by ''Princess Mononoke'' and ''Never Cry Wolf'' and said that he wanted to present a more positive image of wolves to young children to counter the animals' often negative cultural perception, while also acknowledging their dangerous side inherent in nature. He also said that the Loth-wolves personified a duality of the light and dark sides of the Force. ===Concept art gallery=== {{Gallery |source= |storyboards= |concept= File:AhsokaWolf-DaveFiloni-1.jpg|Sketch of Ahsoka Tano riding a wolf drawn by Dave Filoni during the development of ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' File:AhsokaWolf-DaveFiloni-2.png|Another sketch of Ahsoka Tano riding a wolf drawn by Dave Filoni during the development of ''The Clone Wars'' File:Dave-Filoni-wolf-sketch.jpg|Another sketch of Ahsoka Tano and a wolf drawn by Dave Filoni around June 2017{{Twitter|dave_filoni|status/872631916775657474|[[Dave Filoni]]|date=2017-06-07|quote=It might be my Birthday, but here is a gift, and perhaps a clarification, for you. May the Force be with you! - Dave|nolive=1}} File:HighRepublic-PhilNoto.jpg|A Loth-wolf appearing in concept art by [[Phil Noto]] for the ''[[Star Wars: The High Republic]]'' multimedia project{{SW|url=news/5-things-we-learned-about-star-wars-the-high-republic|text=5 Things We Learned About ''Star Wars: The High Republic''}} |digital= |in-progress= }} ===Discrepancies=== In the [[2014]] novel ''[[Servants of the Empire: Edge of the Galaxy]]'', [[Beck Ollet]] states to [[Zare Leonis]] that prior to the time of the Galactic Empire, one would still carry a blaster to ward off Loth-wolves when planting the orchards for [[jogan fruit]]. Author [[Jason Fry]] stated in [[2016]] that Ollet was most likely talking about the time of his [[parent]]s or grandparents, but liked the line to give Lothal history.{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/153521983311/notes-edge-of-the-galaxy-pt-2|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=Notes: Edge of the Galaxy Pt. 2|date=2016-11-22|quote=I liked the little detail about needing blasters to keep off the Loth-wolves. Beck's probably talking about his parents' or grandparents' time, but that line gives Lothal some history and makes the sense of loss deeper.}} This information, however, would seem contradictory to the later introduced idea that Loth-wolves had not been seen in 100 years and were considered extinct, as certainly by the time of Ollet's parents even the most wary farmer would be unlikely to carry a blaster to ward off a predator which had been for so long believed extinct. It is likely, however, that Fry wrote the line before the exact details of the last appearance of Loth-wolves on Lothal was determined. It may also be that Ollet's grandparents encountered Loth-wolves as teenagers or young adults since an 100 years average lifespan would not be out of the question for humans in the Star Wars universe. The art book ''[[The Art of Star Wars Rebels]]'' identifies the wolf head symbol in [[Rex's AT-TE]] as depicting a Loth-wolf. However, the symbol had already appeared years prior as the symbol of [[Clone Commander]] Wolffe and his [[104th Battalion|104th "Wolf Pack" Battallion]] in ''The Clone Wars''.{{TCW|R2 Come Home}} '''Maalraas''' or '''Nighthunters'''<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|272|maalraa}}</ref> were a [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of predatory quadrupeds. Nighthunters hunted in packs, using long claws and powerful fanged jaws to disable their victims. Using [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to cloak themselves, they made themselves nearly indistinguishable from the darkest shadows; only extremely well-trained [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] or [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] could recognize their silhouettes. Their hides and bones were heavily resistant to [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]] as well as intense heat.<ref name="TJP" /> A population existed on the forest moon of [[Dxun/Legends|Dxun]]<ref name="kotor2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> in the [[Japrael system/Legends|Onderon system]] and possibly [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]] itself. Maalraas had huge fangs that protruded from their round heads, and were possibly the ancestors of nighthunters. Maalraas hunted in packs, primarily preying upon [[cannok]]s, although if there were too many of them the cannoks could drive the predator away or even kill it. Maalraas were in turn preyed upon by the [[Zakkeg/Legends|zakkeg]]. In [[3951 BBY]], [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] warriors living on the moon found maalraas to be harsh prey to such a degree that having to clear out a number of them was almost considered a true challenge.

Easy to train from infancy or from older ages, Nighthunters were utilised as loyal guard beasts and were exported from their unrecorded home world by crime syndicates as well as other wealthy individuals willing to trade on the black market.<ref name="TJP" /> While plentiful at the time of the Old Republic era, by the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], they were thought to be extinct, but at least one still survived on [[Parein II 4/Legends|Parein II 4]]. When the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Valin Draco]] was dispatched to the world, he was attacked by the beast and was nearly killed, until at last he won the upper hand. Nursing the wounded nighthunter back to health, he named it [[Crant]], and kept it as a pet. Draco was seduced to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] during the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] and joined the [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitorius]], keeping Crant by his side the entire time. When Draco was sent to the [[Almas Academy]] to capture [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Vhiin Thorla]], he ordered Crant to watch over the captured Jedi. While Draco was away, Crant was killed by members of the [[Alderaanian Resistance]] sent to free Master Thorla.<ref name="Echoes of the Jedi">{{DoD|Echoes of the Jedi}}</ref>

'''Manka cats''' were a [[feline]] predator [[species]] with a pack instinct found across the [[mountain]]s and grasslands of several [[Core Worlds]], with the largest population living in the mountains of [[Alderaan]]. With that [[planet]]'s [[Destruction of Alderaan|destruction]], the species had had its numbers thinned considerably, although they were not yet truly endangered.<ref name="Savage Spirits" />

These creatures ranged from 1.5 to nearly 2 [[meter]]s in length, although they had low-slung bodies for hiding in tall [[grass]] or among rock formations. Manka cats were also distinguishable by the thick manes of fur around their necks, and the two sets of menacing, forward-jutting tusks in their lower jaws.<ref name="Savage Spirits" />

'''Mastiff phalones''' were a [[Sentience|non-sentient]] [[species]] of large [[Bird|avian]] quadrupeds that were native to the savannas of [[Maridun]]. As [[Diet|carnivores]], they were dangerous predators.<ref name="JC" />

==Biology and appearance==
Mastiff phalones were a [[Sentience|non-sentient]] [[species]] of [[Bird|avian]]<ref name="TCWS1-Bestiary" /> with a long body and four legs. They had a coat of gray feathers with dark-blue markings.<ref name="JC" /> While they had the remnants of wings visible at their front legs, their powerful limbs ended in long claws. They also had manes of dark feathers and a long feather-like tail and resembled a [[griffin]]. The mastiff phalones were fast runners and their strong limbs with claws and their toothy beaks made them dangerous [[Diet|carnivorous]] predators on<ref name="TCWS1-Bestiary" /> the [[grass]] plains of their native [[planet]] of [[Maridun]].<ref name="Ultimate" />

==History==
In [[21 BBY]],<ref name="Date">{{TCWcanondates|113}}</ref> several mastiff phalones ambushed several [[clone trooper]]s under [[Jedi]] [[Jedi General|General]] [[Aayla Secura]], [[Jedi Commander|Commander]] [[Ahsoka Tano]], and [[Clone Commander|Commander]] [[Bly]], who had crashed on Maridun, killing clone troopers [[Lucky]], [[Flash]], and [[Cameron]]. Another also attacked Captain [[Rex]] as he protected a badly wounded General [[Anakin Skywalker]] at their ship's crash site. Rex shot one of its feet, frightening it off. A pair of mastiff phalones then went for Rex and Skywalker. Rex killed one, but the other charged at him and destroyed Skywalker's shelter. As it prepared to kill Skywalker, Tano and Rex, with the help of the the native [[Lurmen]] [[Wag Too]], tied up the mastiff phalone's leg and left it alive.<ref name="JC" />

At some point, [[Garnac]] and [[Garnac's hunting guild|his hunting guild]] had mounted a full mastiff phalone in the bowels of their [[Ubrikkian Floating Fortress|mobile base]].<ref name="WH">{{TCW|Wookiee Hunt}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The mastiff phalones first appeared in the episode "[[Jedi Crash]]" of the first season of the animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', released in [[2009]].<ref name="JC" /> Sketches of the creatures were done by [[Wayne Lo]] and finished on [[September 11]], [[2007]] with the title "Mastif Phalone - Turns".<ref name="JC-EG">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/jedi-crash-episode-guide|text="Jedi Crash" Episode Guide | The Clone Wars}}</ref> A piece of lightning concept art featuring one of the creatures attacking a clone trooper at the camp at night was also created by [[Matt Gaser]].<ref name="Artof">''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''</ref>

The '''mastiff phalone''', also known as '''mastif phalone''',<ref name="GaW" /> was a large, aggressive, carnivorous bird native to the savannas of [[Maridun/Legends|Maridun]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Mastif_phalone_pair.png|thumb|left|250x250px|A pair of mastiff phalones stalking prey]]

The top predators of [[Maridun/Legends|Maridun]],<ref name="TCWCE" /> mastiff phalones were quadrupedal pack hunters<ref name="Jedi Crash" /> about two meters long.<ref name="TCWCE" /> As flightless [[Bird/Legends|avians]]<ref name="GaW" /> mastiff phalones had turkey-like heads<ref name="DTBK" /> with a sharp beak, and a mane of large brown feathers.<ref name="Jedi Crash" /> Males used the feathers in courtship displays.<ref name="TCWCE" /> They had a muscular build with sharp talons large enough to wrap around a man's waist.<ref name="Jedi Crash" /> They were nearly as large as a [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]] and impossible to domesticate.<ref name="GaW">''[[Galaxy at War]]''</ref>

They tended to hunt in groups of two or more and used the tall grasses of Maridun's savannas as cover.<ref name="DTBK" /> They were fierce but tended to retreat from an attack if the prey was too powerful, only to later attack the same prey again.<ref name="Jedi Crash" /> When sufficiently agitated, a mastif phalone could be more dangerous than a [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]] and just as hard to bring down.<ref name="GaW" /> The immigrated [[Lurmen/Legends|Lurmen]] had found a peaceful way of dealing with them by a group effort of having several Lurmen distract the mastiff phalone, while one of the group took a rope and tied it around the its legs, immobilizing the creature. The Lurmen later released the captive mastiff phalone back into the wild.<ref name="Jedi Crash" />

==History==
Mastiff phalones descended from flying creatures, with their wings evolved back into powerful limbs.<ref name="TCWCE" />

The [[Amani/Legends|Amanin]] of [[Maridun/Legends|Maridun]] frequently captured mastif phalones and imprisoned them, starving them and mistreating them while in captivity. Once the mastif phalone was sufficiently crazed, the Amanin released the creature in or near enemy encampments, where it went berserk, attacking anything it saw.<ref name="GaW" />

At least a mastiff phalone was hunted and killed by [[Garnac's hunting guild/Legends|Garnac's hunting guild]]. Its pelt was later placed in their [[Ubrikkian Floating Fortress]].<ref name="Wookiee Hunt">{{TCW|Wookiee Hunt}}</ref>

A group of mastiff phalones ambushed the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] party of [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]], [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]], [[Bly/Legends|Bly]] and three [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]], One also attacked [[Rex/Legends|Rex]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] at their crash site. Rex narrowly escaped this attack, and allowed it to run off and bring back a second mastiff phalone, both of which attacked the crash site. Rex killed one with his blaster, but the second evaded the blaster fire. The mastiff phalone destroyed Skywalker's tent and prepared to kill Skywalker. Tano, Bly and a Lurmen healer named [[Wag Too/Legends|Wag Too]] then arrived. As Ahsoka went to strike down the beast, Wag stopped her with a warning and tied a rope to its legs. Together with Ahsoka and Rex, they pulled the rope, tipping the creature on its side to be tied up.<ref name="Jedi Crash">{{TCW|Jedi Crash}}</ref>

'''Mastmots''' (a.k.a. '''motmots''' in some [[Whiphid/Legends|Whiphid]] dialects) were massive, thick-furred, quadrupedal [[ungulate]]s with two nasal horns, two long tusks, long ears, and a dorsal hump over the shoulders.

Herd-dwelling herbivores, they lived on the harsh, frigid world of [[Toola/Legends|Toola]]. The indigenous [[Whiphid/Legends|Whiphid]] people hunted the mastmots, using the body parts for food, clothing, shelter, and tools. Their tusks were often made into necklaces.<ref name="Let Us Prey: The Whiphid's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=Let Us Prey: The Whiphid's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref>

The mastmots could be domesticated as riding mounts, and were so used by [[Clone Commander/Legends|Clone Commander]] [[Keller (clone commander)|Keller's]] [[Keller's unit|forces]] on Toola during the [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]].

'''Mawvorr''' were a hostile, [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] group of [[Species/Legends|species]] found throughout the [[The galaxy/Legends|Galaxy]]. The group included [[crysfang]]s, native to [[Voss]], [[felshade]]s, also known as bog mawvorrs, native to [[Zakuul]] and [[Dxun/Legends|Dxun]], and multiple subspecies of [[mewvorr]], which were smaller in size and often kept as pets during the wars between the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]] and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="TOR" />

Mawvorr were four-legged, typically carnivorous<ref name="codex" /> creatures. They had distinctive four-eyed heads with multiple rows of teeth, high nostrils, two spiky appendages on the both sides and, with an exception of Stunning mawvorrs, two big plates, in addition to four on their backs. The plates of several mawvorr species were glowing, revealing the vessels inside; such were called chromatophore plates. All limbs of a mawvorr had three digits ending with big claws, and their tails and bellies were covered in plates.<ref name="TOR" />

The '''painted spat''' was a subtype of [[carrion spat]], an [[Bird/Legends|avian]] creature native to the [[Corellian system/Legends|Corellian system]].<ref name="SWG:TTE" /> A [[Mutant|mutated]] variant,<ref name="SWG:P18" /> this creature was larger, stronger and more resistant to average carrion spat. Somewhat similar in appearance to the [[carrion spat]]s of [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], the painted spat differed: The coloration of the skin was much darker with pronounced horizontal stripes along the back; the bony structure protruding from the mandible was not, from appearance, a true beak (the jaw did not resemble a beak at all, rather, resembling a reptilian jaw).<ref name="SWG:TTE" />

==History==
The existence of the painted spat was first reported on [[Talus/Legends|Talus]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="SWG:P18" /> In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline">{{StarWarsGalaxiesDate}}</ref> adventurous [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] traveled to Talus in order to hunt painted spats. At least three of these animals were seen roughly 3,500 meters from [[Nashal Starport]].<ref name="SWG:TTE" /> Their large 'beaks' were sometimes used as trophies.<ref name="SWG:TTE" /><ref name="SWG:TC">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=collection|Trophy Creatures}}</ref>

Painted spats were later spotted on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] as well. After the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the painted spat [[Gravefeather]] and its pack of enraged carrion spats attacked [[Farm/Legends|farms]] on the outskirts of [[Coronet City/Legends|Coronet City]], such as [[Pol Handerin]]'s [[Pol Handerin's farm|farm]].<ref name="SWG:HFPH">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=general|Help Farmer Pol Handerin|Corellia}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Painted spats appeared in the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'', a [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|massively multiplayer online roleplaying game]] developed by [[Sony]] Online Entertainment and published by [[LucasArts]],<ref name="SWG:TTE" /> prior to the [[Star Wars video games|game's]] closure on [[December 15]], [[2011]].<ref name="Shutdown">{{SonyCite|url=playerinfo|text=IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ''STAR WARS'' GALAXIES™}}</ref> Painted spats were added to the game with the "[[W:c:swg:Publish 18 Notes for 15 Jun 2005|Publish 18]]," released on [[June 15]], [[2005]].<ref name="SonyCite-Publish 18.0">{{SonyCite|url=content.jsp?page=archive%202005#june|text=Publish 18.0}}</ref>

{{Top}} {{Otheruses}} {{Expand|all sections}} {{Species |image=[[File:Rancor-SWE.png]] |name=Rancor |designation=[[Sentience|Semi-sentient]]''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' |class=[[Reptile]]{{SWE|characters|rancor|rancor}} |subspecies=*[[Jungle rancor]]{{Databank|rancor|Rancor}} *[[Rage rancor]]''[[Star Wars: Commander]]'' *[[Shadow rancor]] |races= |height=*4.2 [[meter]]s {{C|14 [[Foot|feet]]}} *5 meters |length= |wingspan= |mass=1,650kg {{C|3,638 lbs}}''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]'' |skincolor=*[[Color|Brown]]{{Film|VI}} *Dark blue{{TCW|Bounty Hunters (episode)}} *Gray |haircolor= |feathers= |eyecolor=*Black *Brown{{BOBF|Chapter 3: The Streets of Mos Espa}} *Green |distinctions= |lifespan=Up to 80 [[standard year]]s {{C|in captivity}}''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian Visual Guide]]'' |origin=[[Dathomir]]''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]'' |habitat=*Grottos **Plains |diet=[[Diet|Carnivore]] |language= }} {{Quote|Rancor are emotionally complex creatures.|Boba Fett's rancor keeper|}} '''Rancors''' were very large, [[Sentience|semi-sentient]] [[Reptile|reptilian]] [[Diet|carnivores]] [[Homeworld|native]] to the [[planet]] [[Dathomir]], although they were also introduced to and present on [[Felucia]], [[Tatooine]], [[Ottethan]]''[[Star Wars: Creatures vs. Aliens]]'' and [[Koboh]]. Rancors were often seen as mindless, violent creatures, due to their extensive use as fighters across the galaxy, but were also capable of being trained and bonding well with their handlers and acquaintances. ==Biology and appearance== [[File:Muchi-Rampage.png|thumb|left|250px|Muchi, an adolescent female rancor]] Standing around five [[meter]]s tall, with their long arms, clawed fingers, immense, toothy jaws, and [[armor]]ed hides (which could withstand much [[blaster]] fire), rancors were a sight to behold, and made formidable predators; however, they were not inherently vicious to [[Sentience|sentient]] life, despite their infamous and often-intimidating outbursts when threatened or antagonized. A subspecies known as the [[jungle rancor]] populated the planet [[Felucia]]. [[Rage rancor]]s were taller than other rancor subspecies, and had an even nastier temperament. [[Shadow rancor]]s, named for their darker hides, had a notorious penchant for destruction. The proper plural term for a group of rancors in [[Galactic Basic Standard]] was a ''crash''.''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: Expanded Edition]]'' Rancors had red [[blood]]; when the [[Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] cut into a rancor enhanced via the [[cyberanimate]] program, blood flowed from its body instead of the wound cauterizing.[[Darth Vader (2015) 22|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 22]] ==Behavior== {{Quote|The Rancor is a truly marvelous opponent. They're not very bright, but they more than make up for that with their ferociousss strength.|The Trandoshan hunter Charr|''[[Star Wars: Hunters]]''}}
[[File:Unidentified-rancor-TBoBF.png|thumb|250px|right|Boba Fett's rancor]]
Rancors adhered to a social hierarchy, where an alpha was dominant over the other rancors until otherwise defeated. Despite their massive size and extremely intimidating appearance, the creatures were, inherently, benign. Wild rancors were eventually domesticated by the [[Nightsisters|Witches of Dathomir]], using [[witch]]craft and dark [[Magick|force magick]], though they still were formidable animals with a short fuse that could be provoked easily into a violent mood.''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]'' Though they were often bred for fighting or battle purposes, rancors could be very loving to their owners and handlers if trained and properly socialized. Rancor younglings tended to be very energetic and blissfully unaware of their own strength and its effect on others, but they could be easily soothed with a chewing bone or a favorite toy; once they were taught basic obedience, young rancors could calm easily and grow to be very gentle, protective companions.{{GalacticPals|Rancor}} The mouth and [[Tooth|teeth]] of rancors were often cleaned by scavenging [[Unidentified blue Dathomir bird|birds]], the giants simply laying in-wait for the avian cleaners with their mouths open. However, with larger lifeforms, rancors would [[Diet|eat]] anything that they were capable of swallowing.{{GoC|Rancor}} ==History== ===Pre-Clone Wars=== {{Quote|The Force protects me, ''Terec''.''"
«''A pity the same cannot be said for your ''rancor''. The beast is ''corrupted''.''»
«''Myarga! That was a living being!''»
«''Bleeding hearts rarely win wars, Marshal. You would do well to remember that.''»|Avar Kriss and Myarga Anjiliac Atirue|[[The High Republic (2021) 6|''The High Republic'' (2021) 6]]}} [[File:HuttJediAlliance-2021THR6.jpg|thumb|left|300px|In response to the Drengir threat, Jedi rode rancors into battle alongside the Hutt Clan's forces.]] Rancors lived on the planet''[[Star Wars: The Dark Side]]'' that would one day be dubbed [[Dathomir]] by the [[Nightsisters]]. Before the arrival of the Nightsisters, however, the planet was home to the [[Fromprath]],''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' who exploited the natural resources of the planet.''[[Star Wars: The Dark Side]]'' Hundreds of [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Clone Wars]], the Nightsisters laid claim to the planet and named it Dathomir. Seeking to claim the planet from the Fromprath and spurred by their exploitation of natural resources, the Nightsisters formed a symbiotic "alliance" with the native rancors in order to drive out their rivals,''[[Star Wars: The Dark Side]]'' whom they successfully forced into [[Exile (punishment)|exile]].''[[Last Shot]]'' The [[Hutt Clan]] used rancors as mounts for its enforcers, such as [[Gamorrean Warrior]]s.[[The High Republic (2021) 4|''The High Republic'' (2021) 4]] During the [[High Republic Era]], when the [[Jedi Order]] and the [[Hutt]]s were forced to make an alliance against the [[Drengir]], the [[Jedi]] of the [[Galactic Frontier]] would ride rancors into battle alongside Hutt forces. In response to the [[slaughter on Daivak]], [[Jedi Master]] [[Avar Kriss]] and [[Jedi Knight]] [[Terec]] rode atop rancors into battle against the Drengir, while Terec's [[Bond-twins|bond-twin]] (and fellow Knight) [[Ceret]] and Hutt leader [[Myarga Anjiliac Atirue]] rode beside them on [[speeder]]s. The Drengir would begin to overwhelm their enemies over the course of the battle, with one managing to extend its tenacle-like vines into the mouth and nostrils of Kriss' rancor, forcing her to jump from the beast as it succumbed to the Drengir infection. To Kriss' horror, Myarga quickly executed the rancor when it began to rise against them. After the Drengir suddenly began to scream out, the battle reconvened, with Jedi Knight [[Keeve Trennis]] infiltrating the species' root-mind. After discovering the location of the [[Great Progenitor]] on the planet [[Mulita]], Terec's rancor reached out and grabbed one of the botanical monsters. The Jedi and Hutts would launch a massive strike against the Drengir during the [[Battle on Mulita|assault on Mulita]],''[[The High Republic: The Rising Storm]]'' in which [[Trandoshan]] Jedi Master [[Sskeer]] rode a rancor into battle. Although Sskeer tried to cut through the vines, his rancor was subdued by Drengir vines. In the end, however, the battle would end victoriously for the Jedi and Hutts, as the Great Progenitor was forced back into slumber.[[The High Republic (2021) 8|''The High Republic'' (2021) 8]] ===Clone Wars era=== [[File:Jungle_rancors.png|thumb|right|250px|The jungle rancors lived on the planet Felucia.]] The jungle rancor subspecies lived on the world of Felucia; after the [[Destruction of the Felucia medical station|destruction of the Felucia Medical Station HCTFF2]], [[Jedi General]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], [[Jedi]] [[General]] Anakin Skywalker, and [[Jedi Commander]] [[Ahsoka Tano]] saw a group of such rancors on planet. While they were careful to not scare the creatures, the jungle rancors lived a relatively peaceful co-existence with the native [[Felucian]] [[farmer]]s.{{Databank|rancor|Rancor}} ===Imperial Era=== {{Quote|A rampaging adolescent rancor is not the distraction I was anticipating.|Tech, on Muchi|{{TBB|Rampage (episode)}}}} After the [[Proclamation of the New Order|rise]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], [[Clone Force 99]] was hired by [[Ciddarin Scaleback|Cid]] to [[Mission to Ord Mantell (Clone Force 99)|rescue]] [[Muchi]], an adolescent rancor on [[Ord Mantell]], though they were not informed she was a rancor. Muchi was released by [[Omega]] in order to help the squad and some [[Slavery|slaves]] escape from a group of [[Zygerrian]] [[enslaver]]s, and [[Echo]] expressed surprise upon discovering that Muchi was the rancor, not one of the slaves. [[File:RancorOnKoboh-Survivor.png|left|200px|On Koboh, Jedi Knight Cal Kestis killed a rancor after the beast attacked him during his search for the missing prospectors.]] In [[9 BBY]], a [[Unidentified rancor (Koboh)|rancor]] killed some prospectors on the planet [[Koboh]]. The rancor was eventually killed by [[Cal Kestis]] when the [[Jedi Knight]] was sent to investigate the prospectors' disappearance. Later on, the latter discovered another rancor in the aptly-named [[Phon'Qi Caverns]], that had apparently lived there for some time, feeding upon those unfortunate enough to incur its wrath, including the [[Bedlam Raiders]]. Cal reacted with noticeable disbelief upon killing the second rancor. An Imperial was tricked by [[Turgle]], who promised a large quantity of [[priorite]] in exchange for [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]]. In truth, Turgle didn't know where to find the mineral when he made the deal, but thought he would figure it out. This didn't happen, but before the Imperial could do anything about the lost time, the two encountered a rancor. The beast allowed Turgle to escape.''[[Star Wars Jedi: Survivor]]'' After the Sith Lord [[Darth]] Vader killed a [[Unidentified Trandoshan (Cylo-V's warrior)|Trandoshan]] enhanced via the [[Cylo Directive]]'s [[cyberanimate]] program, the Cylo Directive instead implanted the cyberanimate into a rancor.[[Darth Vader (2015) 21|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 21]] The system connected directly to the creature's brain to try and circumvent any weakness it could be faced by. In particular, the rancor was equipped with neural dampeners to prevent it from feeling pain, adrenal stimulants, and a plate-reinforced thorax.[[Darth Vader (2015) 22|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 22]] In the lead up to the [[Cylo Hijacking|hijacking of the ''Executor'']], by which point the rancor was the most recent creation of the labs, the cyborg creature was unleashed against Vader by [[Doctor]] [[Tulon Voidgazer]] in what she dubbed [[experiment 428]]. The rancor approached Vader via [[vector e]] on her order and did not react when Vader cut off some of the creature's hand, as per its neural dampeners, before rushing Vader in a rage upon being shocked by its adrenal stimulants. While Voidgazer regarded that as an unsipirising response, she was pleased by the thorax resisting Vader's [[Force choke]] attack. All the same, once she explained the system, Vader bested the beast by throwing his lightsaber into its brain, killing it. [[File:Rancor-RotJAVA.png|thumb|right|202x202px|Jabba owned a pet rancor named Pateesa.]] A massive rancor named [[Pateesa]]''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]'' was kept as a pet by [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba]] the [[Hutt]] in a shadowy chamber beneath his [[Boba Fett's Palace|palace]] court, to which he fed his enemies or any who displeased him. During the [[Rescue of Han Solo|mission]] to rescue [[Han Solo]], Jabba dispatched the young Jedi Knight [[Luke Skywalker]] into the pit. After the terrifying creature ate [[Jubnuk|one]] of Jabba's Gamorrean guards, the young Jedi defeated the rancor to the shock of all watching. Pateesa's human handler, [[Malakili]], mourned the rancor's death, while an outraged Jabba ordered the public execution of the Jedi and his friends. ===Post-Imperial Era=== [[File:BobasRancorvsScorpenek-Displate.png|thumb|left|300px|Boba Fett rides his rancor as it tears apart a scorpenek droid.]] In [[9 ABY]],{{BoBFDate}} the Hutts known as [[The Twins]] presented a [[Boba's rancor|rancor]] to [[Daimyo]] [[Boba Fett]] on [[Tatooine]] as tribute and an apology for sending the [[Wookiee]] [[gladiator]] [[Krrsantan]] to [[assassin]]ate Fett. The rancor was equipped with blinders, which its [[Unidentified rancor keeper|keeper]] explained was because a rancor would "imprint" on the first [[human]] it saw. Boba removed the rancor's blinders and began to bond with his new creature, asking the rancor keeper to teach him to ride the rancor as the Witches of [[Dathomir]] had. When the [[Pyke Syndicate]] began using Tatooine as part of their [[spice]] trade, Fett met with Mos Espa's criminal leaders at his palace to try to convince them to join him against the Pykes. During the meeting, Fett's guests were surprised at the rancor that was just below them.{{BOBF|Chapter 4: The Gathering Storm}} During [[Battle of Mos Espa|the battle]] that took place in Mos Espa, Fett and his allies were being outnumbered by the Pykes, which was made worse when the Pykes brought in [[Scorpenek annihilator droid|Scorpenek droids]] equipped with deflector shields, against which their weapons were nearly useless. To balance the fight, Fett withdrew from the battle and returned riding his rancor,{{BOBF|Chapter 7: In the Name of Honor}} using his bond with the creature and its species' legacy to instill fear into the Pyke forces.{{InsiderCite|221|A Certain Point of View}} The rancor's appearance changed the course of the battle, with the creature, interestingly, showcasing a superior combat style to the Scorpenek units. [[File:BobasRancor-CGSWG.png|thumb|300px|right|Boba Fett rode his rancor into battle defending Mos Espa.]] When bounty hunter [[Cad Bane]], Fett's former mentor and rival who was working for the Pykes, arrived, the rancor was scared away by Bane's flamethrower, and Fett fell from his perch on its back. Without Fett to keep the beast under control, the rancor began to destroy the city. [[Mandalorian]] bounty hunter [[Din Djarin]], who had been recruited by Fett, faced the rancor and was nearly killed, but before the rancor could kill him, [[Din Grogu|Grogu]], a Force-sensitive child of [[Yoda's species|Yoda's race]] who was in Djarin's care, placed himself between the two and used the Force to [[Taming beasts|calm]] the beast and put it to sleep, which Grogu also did alongside the rancor due to the tiredness caused by the act.{{BOBF|Chapter 7: In the Name of Honor}} In 9 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]],{{HuntersDate}} the [[Trandoshan]] [[Hunter (Grand Arena)|Hunter]] [[Charr]] owned an outfit of rancor bones, which he wore during the [[Hunters of the Outer Rim]] tournament at the [[Grand Arena]] on the planet [[Vespaara]]. When the [[Supreme Leader]] of the [[First Order]] and [[Ren|Master of the Knights of Ren]], [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]], went to a fortress belonging to [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder]] on [[Tatooine]] while learning about the past of his grandfather, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], in [[34 ABY]], he faced off against guards of the fortress who were riding two rancors. Ren killed one of the beasts by piercing its skull with [[Kylo Ren's lightsaber|his]] [[lightsaber]] and incapacitated the other by cutting off its left leg, which caused the [[death]] of the guard standing on it, being crushed by the rancor against the fortress.[[Legacy of Vader 2|''Legacy of Vader'' 2]] ==Behind the scenes== [[File:Rancor_suit_btm.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The rancor was originally to be portrayed by a man in a suit.]] The concept for the rancor in ''Return of the Jedi'' was described by its creators as "a cross between a [[Wikipedia:bear|bear]] and a [[Wikipedia:potato|potato]]."''[[Empire of Dreams: The Story of the Star Wars Trilogy]]'' [[George Lucas]] requested the rancor be "the best" Godzilla-like monster to ever be created, as recalled by [[Phil Tippett]]. Much like Godzilla,''[[From Star Wars to Indiana Jones: The Best of the Lucasfilm Archives]]'' the rancor was first to be played by an actor in a suit. Specifically, the costume called for two actors: one actor controlled an arm, whereas the other controlled the other arm and the rancor's body. After costume tests,{{InsiderCite|222|Together Again, Huh?}} no one was satisfied with the results even though shooting was scheduled to begin in several days. Visual effects supervisor [[Dennis Muren]] had believed the team was on route to a good end product with the suit, especially after lighting, cutting, and camera angles were factored in. However, it was [[George Lucas]] himself who decreed the design was not working and would not in the final film. After plans for suit actors to portray the rancor fell through, Tippett and company—as recalled by puppeteer [[Tim Rose]] to [[Star Wars Insider|''Star Wars'' Insider]]—had intended for the rancor to be portrayed by [[Wikipedia:Go motion|go-motion]], a form of [[Wikipedia:Stop motion|stop motion animation]]{{BookCite|author=Sawicki, Mark|container=Chapter 7: Animate Monsters|title=Animating with Stop Motion Pro|publisher=CRC Press|date=2012|isbn=9781136135897}} that creates smoother results than traditional stop motion, until Tippett saw what Rose's work on Ackbar. Additionally, as noted by Insider in an interview with Muren and fellow ''Return of the Jedi'' visual effects supervisor [[Ken Ralston]], there was not enough time in production to film the rancor as a go-motion or stop motion character. In the end, turning to a puppet was a simpler solution that worked with the time constraints. Both interviews were published in [[Star Wars Insider 222|''Star Wars'' Insider 222]] as "[[Inside the Mind of the Puppetmaster]]" and "[[Together Again, Huh?]]," respectively. In his interview, Muren recalled that the team had looked for other ways to perform the rancor before finally settling on rod puppetry. According to the Rose, seeing Rose's work on [[Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar]]—whose head Rose puppeteered in close-up shots for the film—and enjoying it so much "influenced" Tippett's decision to change course for puppetry. In the end, the rancor was made as a rod-operated puppet. The puppet was operated by Rose, who specifically described the rancor as an act of [[Wikipedia:Bunraku|''Bunraku'' rod puppetry]].{{InsiderCite|222|Inside the Mind of the Puppetmaster}} It was filmed with a high-speed camera to slow its movements down to give the illusion of a much larger creature. Trying to experiment with anything that could to make the rancor, in Muren's words, "more real" and authentic, the team hoped to get the scale and fluidity of the creature across on screen. To those ends, the crew, in addition to shooting it at high speeds, filmed the puppet in reverse—with Tippett himself being the one to move the rancor puppet backwards—and at extremely low speeds. One shot was done in at least ninety takes over the course of what Muren estimated to be around ninety minutes in order to secure all the "little sequences of frames." During the process, the crew knew what the cuts in the scene would be and just had to fit them into the overall edit. Overall, Muren recalled the experience as them "just [shaking] it up." Had the puppet not worked, Muren reflected that the crew would have been forced to rely on the lengthy process that is stop motion. While Muren did give Tippett credit for the rancor's strong design, he confessed to Insider that, whenever he sees the rancor pit sequence, all he sees is the effort put into it. They were usually born brown, but in special circumstances, such as the [[Taanab mutant rancor|mutant rancor]], [[Jungle rancor/Legends|jungle rancor]], and the [[Bull rancor/Legends|bull rancor]], their color may have differed. Although found on other worlds such as [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]]''[[The Essential Atlas]]''—where they were brought by crashed starships—, [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], [[Ottethan/Legends|Ottethan]], [[Carida/Legends|Carida]], [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]], and [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]], those from Dathomir were said to be stronger and more intelligent than others. They had been used for many things, ranging from mounts for the [[Witches of Dathomir]], to pets for crime lords such as [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], to being a source of food, and as a means of entertainment by dropping someone into its pit. [[Vonnda Ra]] of the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]] used a stuffed rancor head as a chair. In her youth as a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] trainee, [[Hapan]] [[Queen Mother]] [[Tenel Ka Djo]] used two trophy rancor teeth for handles to create both her first [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] and second lightsaber. Rancors were also the source of the delicacy (or at least an edible meal) known as [[raw rancor-beast liver]]. ==Biology and appearance== [[File:Rancor_with_young.jpg|thumb|left|A rancor with young]] {{Quote|My rancor seeks flesh!|A Nightsister|''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''}} Warm-blooded rancors fell into the reptomammal category, along with other creatures such as the [[Wampa/Legends|wampa]]. Rancors were attracted to other rancor mates by a smell, or a pheromone. While it is known that rancors did care for their young—usually born two at a time—they did not suckle and hatched from eggs like those of a reptile. The 3 meter tall hatchlings rode the mother, one dorsal, one ventral, until reaching maturity, though despite this nurturing nature, it was not entirely unheard of for a mother to eat her young.[[Legacy (2006) 15|''Legacy'' (2006) 15]] Rancors walked on two relatively stubby legs, with longer forelimbs utilized for catching prey, though they also walked on all fours at times and had a short tail. A rancor's flat face was dominated by a large mouth full of razor-sharp teeth. Although it had sharp teeth, it would often swallow smaller prey (such as humanoids) whole. The skin of a rancor was tough enough to deflect blaster bolts, making it an efficient killing machine—and an excellent source of leather for expensive vests and boots. At least on Dathomir, rancors had good night vision, but their eyesight was not as sharp as a Human's in daylight. Rancors had a symbiotic relationship with [[gibbit bird]]s, an avian species that would clean their teeth, an action that provided the birds with food and the rancors with a form of "dental hygiene."''[[Galaxy of Fear: Eaten Alive]]'' In certain cases, rancors were sentient enough to be able to form and recite complex oral traditions, such as [[Tosh (rancor)|Tosh]], herd-mother of a rancor family that belonged to the [[Singing Mountain Clan]] on [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]]. [[Tionne Solusar]] recorded one such narrative surrounding a [[Witches of Dathomir|witch]] identified as the fallen [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi]] [[Allya/Legends|Allya]], who lived over six centuries before.[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']] ==History== ===Dathomir=== {{Quote|Come to me, rancor!|Silri|}} [[File:Dathomiri.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Witches on their rancor mounts]] Though they were usually considered unintelligent beasts, the rancors of Dathomir at least were semi-[[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], caring creatures who mourned their family members when they died, and who passed on oral histories of the matriarchal herds into which these were organized. Their native way of life seems to have been very primitive, using their strength and size to hunt live prey across the planet's savannahs—with the planet's Human population at one point becoming their primary prey species; but in the last centuries of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the rancor was "domesticated" by the [[Witches of Dathomir]] (though [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitivity]] was apparently necessary to accomplish the difficult task) and the symbiosis of rancor sow and female rider seems to have played a major role in dictating the subsequent structure of Dathomiri society. According to the rancors' own traditions, the symbiosis began when a warrior-woman met and healed an injured female; by mounting the rancor's back, her sharper eyesight enabled it to hunt better prey during the day, so that it grew in size and status to become a mighty [[herd-mother]]. [[File:SingingMountainRancorTrainer-GH.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A rancor trainer of the Singing Mountain Clan]] By the time of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], most of Dathomir's rancor population lived in symbiosis with the planet's [[Witches of Dathomir]] clans, being used as mounts, and learning to make and use armor and bladed weapons with their help. Rancors of a clan were marked to show clan ownership, but younger ones were not marked and could basically serve as undercover mounts, belonging to no clan.''[[Young Jedi Knights: Shadow Academy]]'' Around the years of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], it was believed that the last herds of untamed mountain rancors were driven into the plains and destroyed; but a few decades later, a wild herd wandered into the [[Great Canyon (Dathomir)/Legends|Great Canyon]], indicating that a population had survived in the vast tracts of Dathomir's surface area that remained unexplored, far beyond the knowledge of the planet's Human population. On Dathomir they would often eat pig-like rodents. ===The wider galaxy=== {{Quote|I had to kill a rancor once. It was a shame—they're such fine creatures.''"
"''Even so, they are dangerous to those who are not their friends.|Luke Skywalker and Tenel Ka Djo, about Jabba's rancor|}} [[File:Rancor_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Jabba's rancor/Legends|Jabba's rancor]].]] The rancor was relatively well known in the wider galaxy, having spread across various planets with early spacefaring civilizations even before the rise of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]]; but the rancor's homeworld had been forgotten, and its sapience was rarely recognized. Among the planets that housed rancor populations were [[Carida/Legends|Carida]], [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]], [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]], [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]], [[Trinta]] and [[Regosh]]. The [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] named the [[Form VI/Legends|Niman]] style of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]] after the rancor. This was a style that was known for being well rounded, with no certain offensive or defensive attributes. This might have suggested something about the rancor's predatory style. On a few worlds like [[Ottethan/Legends|Ottethan]], rancors were used as mounts by warrior clans as they were on Dathomir. Herds of young rancors roamed wild on [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]], descended from those brought by the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]], and some were domesticated as beasts of war by the [[Black Rakata]] under [[The One]]. Several of those rancors attacked Revan after he betrayed the promise given to The One to kill the Elder Rakata. Revan also had to fight his way to the Ancient Temple and to the Elder Rakata's enclave through rancors who surrounded the former and guarded the latter. While stranded on [[Taris/Legends|Taris]], the reformed [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] had to pass a rancor in order to infiltrate the [[Black Vulkars/Legends|Black Vulkars]] base. He did this by placing a synthetic odor that made the rancor think that its prey was nearby within a pile of corpses, where a grenade was placed. The rancor, grabbing what it thought was food, swallowed the grenade, which exploded in its mouth and killed the beast.''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' Thousands of years later [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] encountered more rancors of Lehon while following Revan's path.''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]'' Rancors were perhaps most closely associated with the criminal underworld, where individual creatures were kept as pets, guards and status-symbols. Rancors were occasionally used for gambling matches, pitting one beast against another or unleashing one upon slaves and seeing which one survived the longest. One such gambling ring existed on [[Nar Kreeta]]. Infamous slaver [[Phylus Mon]], who dealt in rancors, also used two crossed rancor claws as the symbol of his organization. Sometimes Phylus Mon used rancors to attack his personal enemies, and sometimes his enslaved Force adepts created illusions of rancors to attack his enemies. Rancors were also kept by such criminals as [[Nirama]],{{LivingForce|Between the Worlds: TopWorld}} [[Hlisk Squin]],''[[Living Force Campaign Guide]]'' [[Borvo]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]], and [[Unidentified Hutt crime lord (Nar Kreeta)|the crimelord]] from Nar Kreeta.''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]'' [[File:Rancor_Hunters.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Hunters trap a rancor specimen]] The [[Felucian/Legends|inhabitants]] of [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]] managed to tame the local rancors in a manner similar to Dathomiri Witches. They also used the rancors as mounts, and the bones of the deceased creatures were made into [[Felucian Skullblade|weapons]]. In addition, they usually painted the rancors with fluorescent paints to make them look more intimidating. These rancors were used by the Jedi [[Shaak Ti/Legends|Shaak Ti]] and [[Maris Brood]]. Several of those rancors were slain by [[Galen Marek]] during his [[Mission to Felucia (Great Jedi Purge)|mission]] in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]].''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'' The [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]] used many rancors with [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]] astride them in their campaign to corrupt [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], most notably Nightsister [[Silri]]'s pet, [[Cuddles]]. Perhaps the most famous such rancor was the [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|one]] owned by [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], who kept it in a pit beneath his palace courts, dropping in victims who displeased him in some way in order to feed it. His rancor was cared for by [[Malakili/Legends|Malakili]], a famous beast tamer who had traveled with the [[Circus Horrificus/Legends|Circus Horrificus]]. Malakili formed an unlikely bond with the animal, even going so far as to sneak the rancor out of Jabba's palace for a run in the desert, and wept when the beast was killed by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]. The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] attempted to exploit the combat potential of the rancor—perhaps not a great surprise given that a fully grown Dathomiri rancor was capable of single-handedly destroying an entire [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|AT-ST]] unit. The word "rancor" was often used in the names of independent [[Starship/Legends|starships]] operating throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].{{GamerCite|1|Shipbuilding Secrets}} ===Subspecies=== [[File:JungleRancor-TCWmag11.png|thumb|right|250px|A jungle rancor]] Many subspecies of rancors existed, both on Dathomir and other worlds. Among the subspecies of Dathomiri rancors were the [[gnarled rancor]] and the [[rancor pygmy]].{{GalaxiesAED}} Offworld breeds had evolved into such distinct subspecies, such as the amphibious [[Tra'cor]] found on [[Socorro/Legends|Socorro]] or the gigantic [[tyrant rancor]]. An extremely rare variant was the [[Bull rancor/Legends|bull rancor]] of [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]], an ancient and near-mythical beast that was marked by its paler flesh, elongated tail and immense horns that sprouted from its massive head. One such rancor was tamed and used as a pet by the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Maris Brood]]. Several subspecies did not evolve naturally, but were instead bred, using either genetic manipulations or [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]]. One such variant was the [[Jungle rancor/Legends|jungle rancor]], which was quite different from its common brethren and was found on worlds such as [[Teth/Legends|Teth]].''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: The Visual Guide]]'' The [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Quorlac Fornayh]] used the Sith Alchemy to create [[Coloi]], a rancor with lighter bones and large wings, who had the skin replaced with black metallic plating that could serve as armor. Only one such creature existed and was subsequently destroyed."[[Shadows in the Force]]" The reborn [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] also kept several alchemically altered [[Chrysalide]] rancors at his [[Emperor's Citadel|citadel]] on [[Byss/Legends|Byss]] in order to defend it.{{SeriesRef}} ''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire II]]'' Other mutant rancors were unique and impossible to classify. In [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]] a mutant rancor was bred by the [[Disciples of Ragnos]], who planned on releasing the beast in [[Taanab/Legends|Taanab]] cities so that during the chaos they could steal arms, credits, and other needed goods. The beast was much larger than normal rancors, had green capsules on its back, could breathe a stream of green toxic gas, and had an unnatural green hue to its skin. However, once released, the rancor began attacking the Disciples themselves, who were unable to stop it, as the [[mutant]] was immune to conventional weapons. Eventually it was killed by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Jaden Korr]], who managed to pin it between a force field and a large crate on a conveyor belt. Another example of a mutant rancor is the [[Undead rancor]], which was mutated by Imperial Bioweapons Project I71A, and resided on Dathomir in the Imperial [[Quarantine Zone (Dathomir)|Quarantine Zone]]. This rancor was later killed by a group of spacers. ==Behind the scenes== [[File:Early_Rancor_Concept.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Early concept art by [[Joe Johnston]], later reused by [[West End Games]] to represent the [[Esoomian/Legends|Esoomian]] species]] The concept for the rancor in ''Return of the Jedi'' was described by its creators as "a cross between a [[Wikipedia:bear|bear]] and a [[Wikipedia:potato|potato]]." It was first to be played by an actor in a suit, but no one was satisfied with the results. The rancor was then made as a rod-operated puppet, filmed with a high-speed camera to slow its movements down to give the illusion of a much larger creature.''[[Empire of Dreams: The Story of the Star Wars Trilogy]]'' A combination of matte painting, cartoon rotoscoping, and CG elements were added around the creation to make it look bigger and more menacing. Some of these changes were later omitted or replaced with CG effects in the 2004 DVD release of the [[original trilogy]]. In contrast to the rancor's classification in other sources, ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'' states they're a hybrid of a crustacean and an arachnid. [[Ben Burtt]], sound designer for Episodes I-VII, said in the [[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'']] that he created the rancor's sounds from The '''rikknit''' was a crustacean native to [[New Plympto/Legends|New Plympto]]. They had eight to twelve legs and lived at the tops of [[hiakk tree]]s. Rikknit spun webs for nests and storage. Female rikknit had ovum sacs connected to their abdomens. The [[Nosaurian/Legends|Nosaurians]] removed these to harvest [[Rikknit egg|their eggs]], which were sold offworld as a delicacy. They also harvested ovum sacks from rikknit and processed them into an addictive substance called [[ji rikknit]].

Rikknits were hunted with [[harvest blade]]s before [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] declared them a protected species.

'''Roggwarts''' were large, predatory [[reptile]]s<ref name="VE" /> with curved horns, long tails, and thick skin from the [[planet]] [[Mustafar]], [[Vendaxa]], and [[Guiteica]]. During the [[Clone Wars]], [[General]] [[Grievous]] kept a roggwart named "[[Gor]]" as a pet.

==Biology and appearance==
Roggwarts are large,<ref name="Lair" /> predatory, [[Sentience|semi-sentient]] [[species|beasts]], standing 4 [[meter]]s tall and weighing a quarter-tonne,<ref name="Falcon 65" /> with massive, vicious,<ref name="Lair" /> flesh-tearing [[Tooth|fangs]]<ref name="VE">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]''</ref> and twin horns that curve forwards from the top of their head,<ref name="Lair" /> and can lure in prey with their sticky projectile [[tongue]].<ref name="Falcon 65" /> They had powerful [[Limb|leg]] muscles,<ref name="VE" /> and a lengthy tail ends with three prehensile graspers used to impale or seize a foe, while their robust muscular bodies can withstand [[blaster]] shots,<ref name="Lair" /> [[Magma|lava]],<ref name="Star Wars 11" /> and even certain [[lightsaber]] wounds. The creature also had long claws on their hands and feet.<ref name="Lair" />

Roggwarts were favorite pets of the [[Kaleesh warrior]]s.<ref name="Monsters of the Clone Wars" />

==Behavior==
The creatures have an aggressive nature, and only those taken from the most young of age are able to be trained as pets or guardians.<ref name="Falcon 65" />

==History==
{{Quote|Give a warm Nar Shaddaa welcome to the last of his kind.... Kongo the Disemboweler!|The announcer in the match between Kongo, a roggwart, and Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Star Wars 11">[[Star Wars (2015) 11|''Star Wars'' (2015) 11]]</ref>}}
Roggwarts were native to the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]]<ref name="Mustafar">{{Databank|mustafar|Mustafar}}</ref> [[Mustafar]],<ref name="Build R2-D2 53" /> [[Vendaxa]],<ref name="German Falcon 65" /> and [[Wild Space]]<ref name="Topps">{{Topps|set=2024 Topps Star Wars Hyperspace|cardname=Roggwarts – Mustafar}}</ref> planet [[Guiteica]].<ref name="German Falcon 65" /> At some point, the roggwarts was taken as trophies by the [[warlord]]s of [[Kaleesh]]<ref name="Falcon 65">{{BuildFalconCite|65|Guide to the Galaxy}}</ref> from their battles with the [[Bitthævrian]] [[homeworld]] of Guiteica.<ref name="German Falcon 65" /> During the [[Clone Wars]], [[General]] [[Grievous]] kept a pet roggwart named [[Gor]]<ref name="Lair" /> as a guard<ref name="VE" /> in his [[Grievous's fortress|castle]] on the [[Vassek 3|third moon]] of [[Vassek]]. Gor was roughly the size of a [[rancor]] and had been enhanced by [[EV-A4-D]] with [[cybernetics]]<ref name="Lair" /> including mechanical arms attached to the creature's back.<ref name="VE" /> Gor was released to attack the [[Nautolan]] [[Jedi Master]] [[Kit Fisto]], the [[Mon Calamari]] [[Jedi Knight]] [[Nahdar Vebb]], and [[Clone Commander]] [[Fil]]. Though Fil was slain after Gor grabbed him with his tail and slammed him into the ground, the roggwart proved to be no match for Master Fisto, who used his [[lightsaber]] to kill the beast.<ref name="Lair" />

On [[Nar Shaddaa]], [[Grakkus Jahibakti Tingi|Grakkus]] the [[Hutt]] ran arena fighting at his palace that, sometime after the [[Battle of Yavin]], featured [[Kongo]] the Disembowler, who was advertised as the last of his kind.<ref name="Star Wars 11" />

[[Crokind Shand]] of [[Kanjiklub]] used a [[heavy bore rifle]] with a reinforced-[[galven circuit]] [[barrel]] and a roggwart [[bone]] rifle butt.<ref name="TFAVD">''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

'''Roggwarts''' were large predatory beasts. A distinguishing anatomical feature were a pair of curving horns growing from the sides of their heads. They had a long tail and thick skin. [[Gor/Legends|Gor]] was a pet roggwart owned by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

==Biology==
Roggwarts were large, horned creatures native to [[Vendaxa/Legends|Vendaxa]], where they are natural enemies of the [[Acklay/Legends|acklay]]. The roggwart's evolutionary adaptation made it ideally suited for taking on single foes, since it rarely encounters more than one acklay at a time. A roggwart stood on its hind legs and used its sharp fangs, wicked claws, and thick tail to subdue its prey. A roggwarts was not terribly cunning, but it was difficult to surprise, retaining its predatory instincts even in captivity.<ref name="gaw" />

==History==
[[File:RoggwartAttack-GAW.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A roggwart attacks clone troopers]]

Roggwarts were believed to be a natural offshoot of the [[Bitthævrian/Legends|Bitthævrians]] species, were created from them through [[Bioengineering/Legends|genetic tinkering]], or the two just happen to look similar due to convergent evolution.<ref name="TCWEG">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars – The Official Episode Guide: Season 1]]''</ref> 

After the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] defeated the Bitthævrians in the [[Invasion of Guiteica]], many Kaleesh warriors took baby roggwarts as trophies. Following the [[Bitthævrian War|Kaleesh-Bitthævrian War]], nearly every Kaleesh [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] owned at least one or two roggwarts as watch-guardians or pets.<ref name="TCWEG" />   

By the times of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="Lair of Grievous" /> [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] had obtained<ref name="gaw" /> and kept a pet roggwart<ref name="Lair of Grievous" /> native from [[Guiteica/Legends|Guiteica]]<ref name="Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> named [[Gor/Legends|Gor]] in his [[Grievous's castle/Legends|castle]] on [[Vassek/Legends|Vassek's]] [[Third moon of Vassek/Legends|third moon]]. Gor was roughly the size of a [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]], and was outfitted with battle armor, including a chest plate with mechanical arms, and helmet. He was released to attack [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]], his former padawan, [[Nahdar Vebb/Legends|Nahdar Vebb]], and [[Clone Commander/Legends|clone commander]] [[Fil/Legends|Fil]], in Grievous' castle. In the end, Gor was defeated by [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]] in Grievous' own home.<ref name="Lair of Grievous" />

'''Rycrits''' were herd animals native to [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]]. They were quadrupeds with short fur, long faces, four nostrils, pointed teeth, and sharp cloven hooves. [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'leks]] raised them for their hides, and as a source of meat (often served as [[rycrit stew]]).

Planets with a substantial Twi'lek population often imported rycrit herds. One such planet was [[Talasea]], though the rycrits there went feral when the last of the Talasean colonists were killed by [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] forces under [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]].

The Twi'lek [[Kur (Twi'lek)|Kur]] ate on one for a month when banished to the nightlands by [[Nolaa Tarkona]]. He used the [[Bone/Legends|bones]] for tools and hide for a blanket.

The '''Sith war behemoths''' were beasts of war used by the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]].<ref name="SWBa" />

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Sith_monsters.jpg|thumb|left|200px|War behemoth amongst other Sithspawn.]]
These large herd beasts were one of dozens of different creatures that were used to augment the battle legions of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]. They were notable for being amongst the most impressive of these animals and were massive creatures that were used to transport troops, carry heavy weapons and break through enemy fortifications. The role given to the behemoth was that seen by grav [[Tank/Legends|tanks]] that were used in more modern armies. These gargantuan quadrupeds stood 12 to 15 meters tall and weighed an average of 10,000 kg. Amongst their features included a tough leathery skin with shaggy fur that covered their necks as well as their bodies. A hard shell was noted as well that protected their backs. Their heads also possessed long, curved tusks and a series of horns that projected upwards.<ref name="SWBa" />

Wild war behemoths tended to travel in small groups of two to four and spent most of their existence searching for food. They were omnivorous in the sense that they ate anything they were able to find which included even carrion or living prey too weak to fight or too slow to escape. Behemoths were not noted for being particularly territorial but did react violently when attacked or threatened. However, amongst those tamed by the Sith, generations of breeding led to them being easily managed by anyone that had skills in animal handling. When amongst a Sith army, the war behemoths were outfitted with gun turrets along with a crewed hut that housed four individuals who lashed the beasts armored back. In addition, they carried three bulky weapons that were equivalent to light [[Repeating blaster/Legends|repeating blasters]].<ref name="SWBa" />

The troop container of a [[Sith dreadnaught|Sith personnel carrier]] was able to hold two war behemoths, though only one was able to exit them at a time.<ref name="TSC">{{GamerCite|5|The Sith Compendium}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:SithWarBehemoth.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A war behemoth.]]
These animals were originally native to the icy world of [[Khar Delba]] where they were originally peaceful herd beasts who only used their long tusks to defend themselves against predators. After being discovered by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]], many of the behemoths were transported to harsh jungle worlds where [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]] was used to transform them into violent omnivores. The result of centuries long breeding programs led to an easily trained species that responded well to commands. Through a program of standard command coding, Sith troops were able to control war behemoths in combat.<ref name="SWBa" />

Through the Sith, these creatures were found on [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]], where they became elements within the Sith army.<ref name="BOS" />
