The '''Sith warbird''' was a [[Species/Legends|species]] of flightless [[Bird/Legends|bird]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Khar Delba]] that was commonly used as an [[Artillery/Legends|artillery]] mount by the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]], a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] species from the world [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Discovery of Korriban|arrival]] of [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Exiles]] on the planet Korriban around [[6900 BBY]], warbirds were a mainstay of the [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] [[Infantry/Legends|infantry]] of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]], and the birds were later used by the [[Sith Empire (Exar Kun)/Legends|Sith Empire]] of the fallen [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] during the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]]. [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] warbirds were notorious for their bad temper, and they typically used their large size to ram and trample down their prey.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:SithWarbird-JATM.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A warbird being approached by a humanoid being]]
[[Sith/Legends|Sith]] warbirds were large, flightless [[Bird/Legends|birds]]<ref name="TSC" /> from the [[Water/Legends|icy]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Khar Delba]]. When fully grown,<ref name="CSWE" /> they stood at approximately six [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height from ground to top of the head, and ten meters long from head to tail.<ref name="TSC" /> In place of wings, warbirds had two<ref name="UA" /> short<ref name="JATM" /> dual-clawed [[Limb/Legends|arms]], and the birds also sported two legs and a large,<ref name="UA" /> blunt [[Mouth/Legends|beak]], which was used for devouring prey. Their feathers ranged from [[Color/Legends|yellow]]<ref name="JATM" /> to yellowish-green in color, and they had two [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], with iris colors ranging from black<ref name="UA" /> to blue.<ref name="BoS" /> The creatures also had extremely thick hides, which allowed hooks and spikes to be embedded into the sides of domesticated warbirds without causing the creatures to come to harm.<ref name="JATM" />

==Behavior==
Sith warbirds were predators and were notorious for their bad tempered nature, attacking anything that they saw as a threat. Though lacking in power, warbirds could move with great speed and maneuverability; they typically used their large size to ram and trample their prey, and they were also known to use their large beaks to gore their enemies.<ref name="JATM" />

==History==
{{Quote|During the same war that birthed the silooth, the Sith introduced the warbird and the war behemoth.|Sorzus Syn|<ref name="BoS" />}}
Warbirds originated on the planet Khar Delba<ref name="CSWE" /> in the [[Stygian Caldera]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> where they inhabited the world's frozen [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]].<ref name="CSWE" /> Khar Delba lay within the bounds of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]],<ref name="TEA" /> a civilization established by the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] [[Species/Legends|species]], and, during the early history of the Empire, the birds were discovered and subsequently domesticated by the Sith.<ref name="BoS" />

In the midst of an [[Unidentified war (Sith Empire)|ancient conflict]] in which the Empire became embroiled, the domesticated warbirds were pressed into [[Ground warfare/Legends|military service]] to be used as [[Artillery/Legends|artillery]] mounts,<ref name="BoS" /> as was common practice for tamed animals within the Empire at the [[Time/Legends|time]].<ref name="TSC" /> By the time of the [[Discovery of Korriban|arrival]] of [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Exiles]] on Korriban<ref name="BoS" /> around [[6900 BBY]] following their [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|banishment]] from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> warbird mounts were mainstays of the [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] [[Infantry/Legends|infantry]] forces employed by the Sith, and the Dark [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Sith alchemist/Legends|alchemist]] [[Sorzus Syn]] mentioned the creatures in a [[Sorzus Syn's chronicle|chronicle]] of her encounters with the Sith.<ref name="BoS" />

The first Sith Empire ultimately [[Second battle of Korriban|collapsed]] in [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> and warbirds were later used by the [[Sith Empire (Exar Kun)/Legends|Sith Empire]] of the fallen Jedi [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] during the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]]<ref name="JATM" /> in [[3996 BBY]].<ref name="NEC" />

==Sith warbirds in the galaxy==
[[File:SithWarbird.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A Sith warbird wearing a battle harness]]
Sith warbirds saw common usage among the military forces of the Sith Empire as battle mounts,<ref name="BoS" /> and when employed for combat purposes, the birds were fitted to carry [[battle harness]]es, which contained a [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] to house the rider and a mounted [[Blaster cannon/Legends|blaster cannon]] supported by a [[Fusion generator/Legends|fusion generator]].<ref name="TSC" /> The Sith used the birds as mobile platforms that were deployed in front of infantry columns to weaken enemy ground-based [[Troop/Legends|troops]]. During the Great Sith War, the creatures were also commonly used for [[Scout/Legends|scouting]] and reconnaissance assignments because, as living creatures, they were less likely to be spotted by enemy detection devices.<ref name="JATM" />

After the end of the Great Sith War, Sith warbirds continued to be found throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], with survivors of the conflict [[Reproduction/Legends|breeding]] on worlds where battles had been fought by the Sith. These wild-once-more warbirds were prone to terrorizing local forms of wildlife that posed little threat to them.<ref name="JATM" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Sith warbirds were created by [[Michael Mikaelian]] and were first mentioned in ''[[The Sith Compendium]]'', an article that appeared in the [[2001]] [[Wizards of the Coast]] magazine [[Star Wars Gamer 5|''Star Wars Gamer'' 5]].<ref name="TSC" /> The warbirds later received a further mention in the [[2004]] [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game|roleplaying]] sourcebook ''[[Ultimate Adversaries]]'', which became the first source to provide a visual depiction of the creatures, in an [[:File:SithWarbird.jpg|image]] by the artist [[Matt Hatton]].<ref name="UA" />

'''Squalls''' were small [[Rabbit/Legends|lagomorphs]] that inhabited the [[Planet/Legends|planets]] of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]]<ref name="AED" /> and [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]].

==Overview==
[[File:Squall_pack_SoR.png|thumb|left|200px|A group of squalls on Chandrila]]
These fur-covered creatures were known for having long [[Ear/Legends|ears]], and a distinctive hopping gait. On average, they weighed 5 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] and reached lengths of 30 to 40 [[Centimeter/Legends|centimeters]]. Squall instinctively seemed to want to be around other non-predatory creatures of any [[Species/Legends|species]], including [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] species. When in the company of other creatures, they typically begged for food or raided unguarded food stores. In the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], squalls were renowned for their cuteness, and even further out, most beings found it hard to see them as anything but adorable. On [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]], squalls were normally allowed to roam in and out of the [[City/Legends|cities]] as they desired. Thus, they were the cause of much traffic trouble and annoyance to offworlders; to reduce this slightly, [[squall maintenance]] was introduced to the government's work budget, which went toward pushing the squall population back out of urban centers just after mating season every [[Standard year/Legends|year]].

Despite the fact Chandrila normally applied strict laws to the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] of animals off world, squalls so commonly wandered aboard [[Starship/Legends|ships]] left unlocked that it generally was not even noted by the local authorities and the very worst a [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] would receive was a small fine. However, it was against the law to kill or capture squalls without a permit, due to the huge off-world trade of squalls as pets or food.

Squalls were incredibly popular and common pets in the Core Worlds, especially since most young [[Gender/Legends|girls]] either had one or wanted one. The market off of Chandrila was not hugely profitable, but was steady due to the species seeming to not breed well away from their home. Despite this, numerous breeds were also found on [[Rori/Legends|Rori]]. As pets, squalls were popular not only with young girls, but also as gifts to loved ones during some romantic festivals. To be pets, squalls had to be domesticated and raised from birth, as despite the fact they could be picked up on the street on Chandrila, wild squall were unlikely to stay with a single being and would sometimes even bite to escape if picked up. Domesticated squalls, on the other hand, didn't seem to try to escape from owners and, if left alone for more than 12 hours, would begin to whine. With such popularity among children, abandonment was a common problem for squall, as on [[Planet/Legends|planets]] other than their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], squall couldn't tell the difference between predators and friendly creatures due to the fact they would have learned such things while growing up in the wild. This commonly led to stray domesticated squall living very short lives.

[[File:Squall.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A squall]]
Squall meat was also very popular, especially in the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]], where upper-class diners enjoyed food imported from the Core Worlds. Given that it was also easily transportable and relatively inexpensive, it was a common dish in both high-end restaurants—where a pair of squall would often be served in a rich sauce under the name [[Chandrilan squall tendermeat|Chandrilian tendermeat]]—and low-end diners, where it would simply be sold as "squall meat" or [[squallburger]]s. Eateries were encouraged to only purchase squall meat with the official [[Chandrilian positive ecology seal]] of approval, which showed that the squall the meat came from had been raised in humane conditions. Squall meat not bearing this seal often came from battery-farmed animals, a problem the Chandrilan government tried to solve by acting more harshly toward the smuggling of large herds of squall. Squall meat was usually stringy, but had a very powerful flavor hard to mask, which made it a perfect food to be [[Poison/Legends|poisoned]], as even some food taster's couldn't taste toxins in squall meat.

A large variety was the '''leviasquall'''.

==Behind the scenes==
The squall that [[Allana Djo Solo|Allana Solo]] followed in the [[Millennium Falcon (novel)|''Millennium Falcon'' novel]] wore a vest and directed her into a small opening. This is an obvious allusion to the White Rabbit in [[Wikipedia: Alice in Wonderland|Alice in Wonderland]].

'''Stintarils''' were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of rapacious [[Rodent/Legends|rodents]] that were native to the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], and dwelt in the mid-to-upper levels of the jungle canopy.

[[File:Sintaril.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A stintaril.]]

The Stintarils had sharp [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]] that could easily puncture and hold on to prey, and a knobby hairless tail that was used for balance. These rodents attacked in swarms, being known for their great speed. Their prey mainly consisted of [[Woolamander/Legends|woolamanders]] and [[Whisper bird/Legends|whisper birds]]. The species was nomadic and, as such, were constantly on the move; even their young, born in litters of four or five, were born in transit.

The metabolism of the stintaril was extremely high, and they had to eat often or risk starving to death within a few hours. Hungry stintarils were known to turn on their own kind as a last resort, cannibalizing the weaker among them in order to survive.

Following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the collector [[Breac Slaus]] tasked a group of spacers to hunt and kill an unreasonable number of stintarils.<ref name="SWG:SS">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=collection|Stintaril Suppressor}}</ref>

The '''tach''' was a small [[Primate/Legends|simian]] creature native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]]. It was more or less a harmless and curious creature. The tach was considered an annoying creature by many of the [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] because of their peculiar tendency to emit a high-pitched yelp.

Tachs were harmless except when a person was sprayed with a mist of tach essence. The essence enraged local tach, inciting a desire to kill the person with the essence on them. Generally, the only reason anyone would spray this essence on themselves is to lure the tach closer to themselves to kill it. Once the tach was dead, the gland near the brain could be removed, and sold for a high price.

Tach glands had all sorts of chemical properties. When powdered, they made an excellent stimulant, and they were also the main ingredient in [[Tarisian ale]]. [[Mission Vao]]'s brother, [[Griff Vao|Griff]], planned on harvesting these tach glands to make Tarisian ale in order to pay his debts to an [[Exchange]] crime lord, but was unsuccessful.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" />

The '''Taozin''' were a type of creature that, as a grub, had a long body with eight [[limb]]s. In [[10 BBY]], the [[crime lord]] [[Dryden Vos]] kept a Taozin grub on display in his [[Dryden's study|study]] aboard his [[Nau'ur-class yacht|ship]], the ''[[First Light]]''. A Taozin grub was also kept in [[Oga's Cantina]] in [[Black Spire Outpost]] on the [[planet]] [[Batuu]] in [[34 ABY]]. The Taozin was placed in [[Water|brine]] that the creature infused with certain qualities. Some [[species]] considered the infused brine a [[Foodstuff|delicacy]] that increased their mental fortitude.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|The grub's brine is an exotic and valuable delicacy to some species who believe it gives them mental fortitude. The liquid is life-preserving and sedating for the grub as it infuses the liquid with certain qualities. It's most likely why the crime lord Dryden Vos kept one handy in his yacht.|Eloc Throno, ''Traveler's Guide to Batuu''|<ref name="Travelers" />}}
The Taozin were a type of creature with a life cycle that included a grub stage. While a grub, the creatures possessed a long,<ref name="Travelers" /> [[Color|white]]-skinned body<ref name="Solo" /> with eight pairs of [[Limb|legs]] clustered at one end below its head, which had black [[eye]]s. If kept in [[Water|brine]] as a grub, the liquid was life-preserving and sedating for the Taozin, which infused the liquid with certain properties.<ref name="Travelers" />

==Taozin in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Travelers often ask me about the strange creatures Oga keeps in her Cantina. No, I'm not talking about the clientele; I'm referring to the ones she keeps behind the bar. In fact, these creatures are hard at work providing key ingredients for some of Oga's most exquisite concoctions.|Eloc Throno, ''Traveler's Guide to Batuu''|<ref name="Travelers" />}}
[[File:Taozin-Vynock-Solo.png|thumb|left|250px|Dryden Vos kept a Taozin (left jar) on board the ''First Light''.]]
By [[10 BBY]],<ref name="Solo date">The Taozin grub that [[Doelsor Triggant]] gifted to [[Dryden Vos]] is shown on display in Vos's study during the main events of ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'', which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[10 BBY]].</ref> the [[crime lord]] [[Dryden Vos]] had received a Taozin grub as a gift from [[Moff]] [[Doelsor Triggant]]. Vos kept the grub in [[suspended animation]] within a transparent sealed jar, which was displayed on a pedestal in his [[Dryden's study|study]] onboard the [[Nau'ur-class yacht|''Nau'ur''-class yacht]] ''[[First Light]]''.<ref name="SoloOG">''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]''</ref>

During the [[First Order]] [[Battle of Batuu|occupation]] of the [[planet]] [[Batuu]] in [[34 ABY]],<ref name="GE date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the [[Battle of Batuu|mission to Batuu]], which includes the [[First Order]] occupation of [[Batuu]], to [[34 ABY]].</ref> the [[Blutopian]] [[Oga Garra]] stored a Taozin in a jar of brine on the top shelf of her [[Oga's Cantina|cantina]] in [[Black Spire Outpost]]. Garra reserved the Taozin for only her most important guests, as some [[species]] considered its brine an exotic and valuable [[Foodstuff|delicacy]], believing that it granted them mental fortitude.<ref name="Travelers" /> In the same [[Standard year|year]],<ref name="Travelers date">{{TravelersGuidetoBatuuDate}}</ref> author [[Eloc Throno]] wrote about both Vos and Garra's Taozin in the [[book]] ''[[Traveler's Guide to Batuu]]'', speculating that the properties of the Taozin brine was why Vos had held one aboard his [[yacht]].<ref name="Travelers" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Taozin.jpg|thumb|right|100px|Taozin first appeared in the Legends continuity.]]
A Taozin first appeared in the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in the [[2018]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|Anthology Series]] film, ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''.<ref name="Solo" /> The creature was then identified in [[Pablo Hidalgo]]'s accompanying reference book, ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]''; however, the book incorrectly labeled an image of a [[dwarf vinock]] as the Taozin grub.<ref name="SoloOG" /> This was rectified when both creatures were correctly labeled in the [[2019]] video "Every Creature in the ''Star Wars'' Movies," which was part of the ''[[Star Wars By the Numbers]]'' series created by [[StarWarsKids.com]].<ref name="YouTube">{{SWKidsYouTube|series=Star Wars By the Numbers|text=Every Creature in the Star Wars Movies|video=liYY0_DcgE8|nolive=1}}</ref>

The Taozin were originally created for the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where they first appeared in [[Michael Reaves]]'s [[2001]] novel ''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''.<ref name="ShadowHunter">''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''</ref> They were later depicted in an illustration by [[R. K. Post]] published in the ''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]'', a [[2002]] Legends supplement to the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' produced by [[Wizards of the Coast]].<ref name="PotJS">''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]''</ref>

The '''taozin''', also known as a "force dragon' was a giant annelid with many arms and legs native to the [[Jungle moon of Va'art|jungle moon]] of [[Va'art]]. Capable of spitting silken webbing to entrap its prey, taozins' natural shell armor was almost completely resistant to [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]]<ref name="POTJ" /> and [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]]. Their translucent body served to diffuse energy based weapons. A lightsaber in contact with the shell could retain enough cohesion to hurt the creature, but not seriously wound it.<ref name="Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter" /> 

[[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] creatures, taozin could interfere with the sense abilities of [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]], making them appear invisible in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="TJP" /> [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] would describe attempting to sense one as "almost like encountering a surface so slick that one could find no purchase on it."<ref name="Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter" />

Finding their way all over [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], taozin were thought to be extinct until [[Darsha Assant]], [[Lorn Pavan]], and [[I-5YQ]] stumbled across one circa [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] while fleeing from Darth Maul in the depths of the [[Coruscant Underworld/Legends|Coruscant underworld]]. The [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] eventually [[Death/Legends|killed]] it by cutting the bridge that he and the taozin were on, letting it fall into the chasm below while Maul escaped.<ref name="Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter" />

[[Taozin amulet|Taozin nodules]] were small, roughly spherical objects taken from the skin of a taozin which could maintain the same Force-disguise that a living taozin could, causing wielders to be nearly undetectable in the force.<ref name="TJP" /> In 32 BBY, I-5YQ took a nodule from the creature they encountered in the depths and gave it to Pavan. Pavan would use it to hide his presence during his unsuccessful assassination attempt on Maul.<ref name="Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter">''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''</ref> Similarly, in [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]], [[Gregar Typho]] obtained a nodule from a [[Kubaz/Legends|Kubaz]] apothecary, while preparing for an attempt to assassinate [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]]. The apothecary considered it a "rare curiosity."<ref name="Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows" />

After the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] came to power in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the members of the [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitorius]] were equipped with taozin amulets, which would mask their presence while on the hunt for rogue Jedi.<ref name="Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref>

'''Thrantas''' were a group of flying [[Species/Legends|animals]] originally found on [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="codex">{{TORcite|type=codex|Thranta}}</ref> While there were multiple species and breeds varying in size and shape, most of them were easily domesticated; with some used for personal travel, others - for massive [[Atmosphere/Legends|air]] ferries,<ref name="Illustarated" /> most thrantas served as air transport. A passenger compartment could be placed on creature's back or around its chest, ranging in size from a single seat to enormous public carriages.<ref name="wildlife" />

Thrantas were buoyed by airsacks under their skin and fed upon small flying creatures and [[airborne zooplankton]].<ref name="wildlife" />

==History==
Most of thranta species were wiped out along with their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] at the hands of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]], when the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]] [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|blew up]] [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="Illustarated" /> However, [[common thranta]]s<ref name="wildlife" /> and [[Balana thranta]]s{{Fact}} survived the [[Death/Legends|extinction]] of most Alderaanian life, due to a few members of their respective species having been shipped to the [[Tibanna/Legends|tibanna]] gas-rich [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]]. There they enjoyed the open skies under the watchful care of the mysterious [[Thranta Rider]]s.<ref name="Illustarated" /> A large breed known as [[giant thranta]]s, larger versions of the common kind, was similarly preserved.<ref name="Anthology">{{[[Alien Anthology]]}}</ref>

Thousands years before, some thrantas were also transplanted to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] but could not acclimatize due to the planet's air pollution.<ref name="codex" /> During the reign of the Galactic Empire, this was tried again, with the same result. Several other attempts at transplantation to other planets proved unsuccessful; only on Bespin did the thrantas thrive, and were a tourist attraction both as wild beasts and in [[Sky rodeo|thranta rodeos]].<ref name="Illustarated" /> Many thranta species were featured at the [[Holographic Zoo of Extinct Animals|Holographic Zoo for Extinct and Exotic Species]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="wildlife" />

==Species==
[[File:Thrantas-woswfg.jpg|thumb|Various thranta species]]
''[[Common thranta]]'' were the most known species of thrantas. Other notable thranta species included:

*''[[Pilotta thranta]]''<ref name="wildlife" />
*''[[Balana thranta]]''<ref name="wildlife" />
*''[[Great thranta]]''<ref name="wildlife" />
*''[[Giant Red thranta]]''<ref name="gsi" />

Often misidentified as a thranta was the [[Aiwha/Legends|aiwha]] of [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], an imported species originally hailing from [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].

'''Tookes''' were [[Species|creatures]] that could be found on the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]] [[Batuu]] in the [[forest]]s near the [[Black Spire Ruins|ancient ruins]]. Tooke tracks were visible in the dirt around [[Black Spire Outpost]] during the [[Battle of Batuu|occupation]] of the planet by the [[First Order]] in [[34 ABY]] and were included in a scavenger hunt created by the [[Amani]] [[Bina]], owner of the local [[Creature Stall]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|Tookes are awake mostly at night. They have large eyes to see better in the dark and can run quickly.|Bina, ''Bina's Guide to the Creatures of Batuu''|<ref name="Creature Stall" />}}
Tookes were small, round, bipedal [[Species|creatures]] that lived in the [[forest]]s on the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]] [[Batuu]]. Their bodies had [[Color|tan]] [[Hair|fur]] and ended in a long tail that terminated in darker brown fur. Tookes had two [[Limb|legs]] that ended in paws with three [[claw]]ed toes that allowed them to run quickly and jump long distances. They had whiskers on their face, a round [[nose]], and their underbelly had two small arms ending in two digits each. Tookes were mostly nocturnal, with their large, black [[eye]]s allowing them to see well in the dark.<ref name="Creature Stall" />

==History==
{{Quote|What do their tracks look like?|Bina prompts younglings to locate tooke tracks in ''Bina's Guide to the Creatures of Batuu''|<ref name="Creature Stall" />}}
[[File:Tooke_tracks.jpg|thumb|right|190px|Tooke tracks along the pathway to Batuu's ancient ruins]]
Two [[Standard week|weeks]] after the [[Battle of Batuu|arrival]] of the [[First Order]] on Batuu,<ref name="GEStaff">{{GEStaff|Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge|formatted=''Star Wars'': Galaxy's Edge|land}}</ref> in [[34 ABY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance]]'', an attraction in [[Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge|''Star Wars'': Galaxy's Edge]], depicts the climax of the [[Battle of Batuu|mission to Batuu]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[34 ABY]]. Thus, the events in ''Star Wars'': Galaxy's Edge, including the distribution of ''[[Bina's Guide to the Creatures of Batuu]]'', can be dated to that [[Standard year|year]].</ref> the [[Amani]] [[Gender|female]] [[Bina]], who owned the local [[Creature Stall]] in [[Black Spire Outpost]], included tookes in her interactive [[Book|guide]], ''[[Bina's Guide to the Creatures of Batuu]]''. Her employees handed the books out to [[youngling]]s nine [[Standard year|years]] old or younger free of [[Currency|charge]]. Participants were tasked with locating the tracks of the creatures, which could be found along [[Savi's Path]] leading to the nearby [[Black Spire Ruins|ancient ruins]] as well as other dirt paths outside Black Spire Outpost. Upon completion of the activity, younglings were rewarded with a token.<ref name="Creature Stall" />

==Behind the scenes==
Tooke footprints were included in themed pathway details in [[Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge|''Star Wars'': Galaxy's Edge]],<ref name="Savi's Path">{{GalaxysEdge|Savi's Path}}</ref> the themed land that opened to guests at [[Disneyland]] Park and [[Disney's Hollywood Studios]] in [[2019]],<ref name="D23">{{D23|url=creatures-droids-and-aliens-meet-the-fantastical-figures-of-star-wars-galaxys-edge|text=Creatures, Droids, and Aliens: Meet the Fantastical Figures of ''Star Wars'': Galaxy's Edge}}</ref> marking the creature's first inclusion in the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]].<ref name="Savi's Path" /> However, the tracks were not identified as tooke tracks until the release of ''Bina's Guide to the Creatures of Batuu''<ref name="Creature Stall" /> in [[February]] [[2020]].<ref name="WDWNT">{{WebCite|url=https://wdwnt.com/2020/02/photos-kids-can-earn-special-token-by-completing-batuu-scavenger-hunt-at-disneyland-resort|text=PHOTOS: New "Bina's Guide to the Creatures of Batuu" Scavenger Hunt Available in Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge at Disneyland|author=[https://wdwnt.com/author/elise-dwight Elise Dwight]|date=2020-02-03|archivedate=20200417222741}}</ref> The [[Tooke/Legends|tookes]] first originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where they first appeared in the [[1999]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars Episode I: The Gungan Frontier]]''.<ref name="Gungan Frontier">[[Star Wars Episode I: The Gungan Frontier|''Star Wars'' Episode I: ''The Gungan Frontier'']]</ref>

'''Tooke-trap plants''' were a [[species]] of carnivorous plant that were native to [[Naboo]]. They were grown by [[Gungan Greenthumb]], four of whom were smuggled to [[Jakku]] by the request of [[Granny Greenthumb]]. The [[First Order]] was made aware of this, and attempted to stop the plants from growing but was unsuccessful.<ref name="LEGO saga">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]''</ref>

==Biology==
Tooke-trap plants were grown from seeds which would sprout into four-leafed seedlings. Fully grown tooke-trap plants possessed a long stalk with a "mouth" on the end, that protruded from a bush that contained eight leaves. They would occasionally hiss.<ref name="LEGO saga" />

==Behind the scenes==
Tooke-trap plants were first introduced in the [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] video game ''[[Star Wars Episode I: The Gungan Frontier]]''. In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[Canon|continuity]], Tooke-trap plants first appeared in the [[2022]] non-canon [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]'', published by [[TT Games]].<ref name="LEGO saga" />

'''Tooke-trap plants''' were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of carnivorous plant that were native to the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]]-occupied [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].

==Biology==
[[File:TookeTrapPlant-TGF.jpg|left|thumb|A tooke-trap plant]]
They were carnivorous plants that possessed between one and four stalks, each with a "mouth" on the end, that protruded from a leafy central bush. Though these plants could survive solely on water and sunlight like a normal plant, tooke-traps also preyed on small rodents and small arthropods (especially insects). Their main prey was the [[Tooke/Legends|tooke]], from which the species derived its common name. Because the fragrance it emitted was identical to that of tooke mating pheromones, tookes found it irresistible. [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] found the carnivorous plants to be excellent house plants.

Tooke-trap plants would sometimes form a symbiotic relationship with [[Shiro/Legends|shiros]], where the reptiles rolled in mud and collected dirt and seeds between shell ridges. From this, tooke-traps grew and flourished in these "soil pockets" creating a symbiotic relationship nicknamed a "[[shiro-trap]]": tooke-traps provided camouflage for shiros against enemies like [[saw-toothed grank]]s, and in return the shiros provided locomotion for their tooke-trap passengers.

Tooke-traps themselves were food for [[clodhopper]]s.

'''Tooke''' were small, hopping [[Rodent/Legends|rodents]] native to the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].

They had large, sensitive [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] for nocturnal activity as well as sensitive whiskers. Like all rodents, the tooke had a high reproductive rate. They would have a litter of eight, and in two weeks, the young would be fully independent and fertile. Tookes fed on swamp nuts and berries.

A common natural enemy for the tookes were [[Tooke-trap plant/Legends|tooke-trap plants]] - the fragrance they let out was identical to tooke mating pheromones and, therefore irresistible. However, tookes had fast reflexes and could often escape at the last moment with an instinctive defensive backflip.

Another predator of the tooke was [[otta]].

On the Gungan frontier, it was discovered that the rodents' flesh was toxic to [[Rancor/Legends|rancors]]. The tooke's delicate tail [[Hair/Legends|hairs]] were plucked by Gungans to create paint brushes.

They occurred on [[Stoga]], providing food there for [[Worrt/Legends|worrts]].

'''Tortons''' were red and green testudines with long legs. They originated on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo's]] moon of [[Rori/Legends|Rori]].

A species called the [[tortur]], almost completely identical to the torton, lived on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Talus/Legends|Talus]]. The only notable difference between the two species was their skin pigmentation. Though not normally aggressive, these massive creatures (equivalent in size to a [[Fambaa/Legends|Fambaa]]) would put up quite the fight when challenged. There also lived pygmy torton variations.

==Biology==
Tortons were [[oviparous]] species from Rori. They were known for their lengthy lifespan.<ref name="SWG:PTC">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=poi|Pygmy Torton Cave|Rori}}</ref>

Torton meat was comestible. The cookbook ''[[Essential Cooking Skills]]'' detailed how to best cook that meat.<ref name="SWG:ECS">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=item|ESSENTIAL COOKING SKILLS}}</ref>

==History==
During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a pack of pygmy tortons lived in a [[Pygmy Torton Cave|cave]] on the [[Naboo/Legends|Nabooian]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Rori/Legends|Rori]].<ref name="SWG:PTC" />

'''Tuk'ata''' were a [[species]] of creatures classified as a [[Sith]] [[Sith warbeast|warbeast]].<ref name="Dooku: Jedi Lost">''[[Dooku: Jedi Lost]]''</ref> Also known as '''Sith hounds''', they could be found on [[Moraband]].<ref name="Galaxy's Edge 4" />

==Biology and appearance==
Tuk'ata were large quadrupedal creatures whose [[limb]]s ended in clawed paws. They boasted a long whip-like tail, a [[mouth]] full of sharp [[Tooth|fangs]], and a row of spines along their back and tail. One tuk'ata was known to possess the ability to leap over twice its height.<ref name="Galaxy's Edge 4" />

==History==
{{Quote|How was I supposed to know the Sith hound wasn't just a legend?!|Doctor Chelli Lona Aphra, to a Shistavanen|<ref name="Galaxy's Edge 4" />}}
At one point, [[Latts Razzi]]'s [[Razzi Syndicate|crime syndicate]] acquired two complete [[Mummy|mummified]] specimens. Those mummies were later confiscated by [[Dryden Vos]] of the [[Crimson Dawn]] syndicate, along with many other goods.<ref name="Smuggler's Guide">''[[Star Wars: Smuggler's Guide]]''</ref>

[[Doctor]] [[Chelli Lona Aphra|Aphra]] [[Mission to Moraband (Dok-Ondar)|entered]] an [[Sith temple (Sword of Khashyun)|ancient temple]] in search for the fabled [[Sword of Khashyun]] some time after the [[Battle of Yavin]] with a crew of [[Shistavanen]], during which she was surprised when she encountered a tuk'ata guarding the [[Burial|tombs]], having believed the species to be mythical at the time. The [[archaeologist]] and the remainder of the crew then lost the final Shistavanen to the hound as they were chased down the hallways before the rogue deceived the beast, leading it to one of the traps laid within the construct and pretending to be injured and immobilized. The tuk'ata took the bait, leaped high towards Aphra and inadvertently triggered a [[laser]] field that proceeded to bring the hound to a halt, allowing Aphra and her [[droid]] companion, [[BT-1]], to escape the [[Sith]] tomb.<ref name="Galaxy's Edge 4" />

The [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] '''tuk'ata''', or '''Sith hounds''', were used for thousands of [[Standard year/Legends|years]] to guard the tombs of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lords of the Sith]] on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]].<ref name="JATM" />

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Tukata-JATM.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A Tuk'ata]]
Tuk'ata were oversized beasts that were bred to be both fearless and relentless where they were tasked with guarding the Sith tombs on Korriban. Their distinctive characteristics included sharp horns, long claws and savage teeth. Tuk'ata were unusually intelligent and were even able to communicate with one another through means unknown. It was claimed that originally the species were non-violent grazing animals before being corrupted by [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]] experiments that awakened latent parts of their brain which transformed them into unnatural abominations. On occasion, random mutations produce some tuk'ata that were able to live for centuries and grew to immense proportions.<ref name="Codex: Tuk'ata">{{TORcite|type=codex|Tuk'ata}}</ref>

Tuk'ata could speak the [[Sith (language)|Sith]] language.<ref name="Ascension" />

Tuk'ata were said to draw nourishment from the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|Dark side of the Force]] itself.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

'''[[Tuk'ata Nobilis|Tuk'ata nobilis]]''': A pair of tuk'ata tamed by the [[Jedi Beast Master]] [[Kanzhei Opli]] three centuries before the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and given to the Jedi Temple of [[Vaklin]], they distinguished from the original pack for their blue eyes in comparison with the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark-sided]] red eyes of a normal tuk'ata. The only two specimens were killed by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="Purge" />

==History==
{{Quote|A creature from another age, a Tuk'ata. The Sith placed them here long ago to guard their tombs. They still perform this task.|Luke Skywalker describing a tuk'ata|<ref name="Invasion" />}}
[[File:Sith_hound.jpg|thumb|right|180px|A Tuk'ata in the [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|Valley of the Dark Lords]].]]
While on Korriban, [[Freedon Nadd]] and an unidentified Dark Lord of the Sith forced [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] to fight several hounds as a test.<ref name="dlots3" /> Tuk'ata were present in the [[Great Temple/Legends|Great Temple]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] when Exar Kun ordered [[Aleema Keto]] and [[Crado]] to destroy the [[Cron Cluster/Legends|Cron Cluster]].<ref name="TSW4">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 4]]</ref> [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] managed to kill one and take a [[Tulak Hord's holocron|Sith holocron]] from its belly. There were also some tuk'ata in [[Tulak Hord]]'s tomb, where the tuk'ata mother lived.<ref name="kotor" /> By the time of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], the valley was flooding with new and more vicious races of tuk'ata and many Sith both students and [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lords]], including Lord [[Renning]], were interested in their biology which made them Force-sensitive.<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] had to deal with them in the [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|Valley of the Dark Lords]] on Korriban.<ref name="pod">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref> Approximately a thousand years later, a Jedi strike team made up of [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], [[Siri Tachi/Legends|Siri Tachi]], [[Soara Antana/Legends|Soara Antana]], [[Ry-Gaul]], and their respective apprentices faced a pack of Tuk'ata when entering the same mausoleum-lined Valley.<ref name="FinalShowdown" /> [[Tol Skorr]], the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Dark Acolyte/Legends|servant]] of [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], would be injured by one that had grown to a monstrous size and would face it years later when he and [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] attempted to raid [[Darth Andeddu]]'s tomb.<ref name="Star Wars Republic 63: Striking from the Shadows">[[Republic 63|''Republic'' 63]]</ref>

Another large tuk'ata guarded a cave on Yavin 4. It was confronted by the Solo children, [[Darth Caedus|Jacen]], [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina]], and [[Anakin Solo|Anakin]], along with [[Lowbacca]], and [[Finn Galfridian]]. It was initially hostile, but retreated back into its cave after Jacen Solo helped heal it.<ref name="Invasion">[[Invasion 2|''Invasion'' 2]]</ref> When [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], [[Ben Skywalker]], Jaina Solo, and [[Vestara Khai]] went to Korriban to search for the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]] they were attacked by a large group of tuk'ata, but before they could attack Vestara communicated with them through the Sith language and told them not to attack.<ref name="Ascension" /> In [[138 ABY]], [[Darth Nihl]] used the Force to bend an attacking tuk'ata's will to his own,<ref name="Legacy48">[[Legacy (2006) 48|''Legacy'' (2006) 48]]</ref> but [[Darth Talon]] killed it shortly afterwards.<ref name="Legacy50">[[Legacy (2006) 50|''Legacy'' (2006) 50]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The tuk'ata first appeared in [[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 3|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 3]],<ref name="dlots3" /> but were unnamed until the publication of [[Daniel Wallace]]'s ''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]''.<ref>{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2012/03/endnotes-for-star-wars-book-of-sith.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: Book of Sith (part 1)}}</ref>

{{Quote|The veermok, of course! Have you seen a more interesting creature? I take every chance I can get to educate others on my findings. Too bad I don't have the time right now!|[[Ronin Lightrunner]], to a spacer|<ref name="SWG:RL">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=herald|Ronin Lightrunner|Naboo}}</ref>}}
The '''veermok''' was a large, ferocious primate native to the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]] and woodlands of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name="Wildlife" />

==Description==
The veermok lived around the fringes of the swamp and woodlands hunting prey, such as [[jimvu]], [[Hrumph/Legends|hrumph]] calves, and [[Narglatch/Legends|narglatch]] cubs, through stealth and surprise. They avoided deep water, as they were weak swimmers. They also had a unique bounding movement that took advantage of powerful upper torso and shoulder rotation, along with strong lengthy arms that dwarfed their skinny hind limbs. A veermok also had powerful, tri-tipped claws for gouging and grabbing.<ref name="Wildlife" />

[[File:VeermokAndJimvu-WSW.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A Veermok hunting a [[Jimvu]]]]
The hair on a veermok's back and chest provided protection and insulation. Their hair rose on their back when alarmed or angered. Hairless lower anatomy allowed for easy hygiene.<ref name="Wildlife" />

Veermoks were generally solitary, unless mating. Mates apparently formed a bond during the time in which they were together. If one mate was killed, the remaining mate would take revenge on whatever or whomever was responsible. They were usually semi-territorial, but not always, defending turf from other veermoks. Females mated once a year, building nests on the ground in a bed of leaves and branches. The veermok had a gestation period of three months. They usually gave birth to twins, which in most cases were immediately abandoned by their mother, unlike the more nurturing [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]]. It appears that in a few unusual cases a mother would care for her offspring, at least for a short time. Forced to fend for themselves, abandoned twins matured quickly.<ref name="Wildlife" />

Veermoks had an unusual resistance to [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]].<ref name="TSL">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>

==History==
Veermok meat was comestible. The cookbook ''[[Essential Cooking Skills]]'' detailed how to best cook that meat.<ref name="SWG:ECS">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=item|ESSENTIAL COOKING SKILLS}}</ref> Veermoks were also popular [[holopet]]s.<ref name="Holopets">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=66920&resource=features|text=Holopets}}</ref> The [[leaping veermok]] was an attack of the [[Teräs Käsi/Legends|Teräs Käsi]] martial art named after the leaping attack of the veermok.<ref name="SG">''[[Shadow Games]]''</ref>
[[File:Veermok-wosfg.jpg|thumb|right|200px|An escaped Veermok on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]]]

During the [[Old Sith Wars]], the [[Systech Corporation/Legends|Systech Corporation]] created a line of [[Systech electric blaster|electrical]] [[Systech static blaster|weapons]] to deal with veermoks by bypassing their resistance to blasters.<ref name="TSL" />

During the last decades of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]], veermoks were transported to [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Hego Damask's]] private moon [[Sojourn (moon)|Sojourn]] for [[Big game hunter/Legends|big-game hunting]].<ref name="DP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

In the years prior to the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], a criminal involved in the illegal activities of [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and [[King/Legends|King]] [[Ars Veruna/Legends|Veruna]] on Naboo was nicknamed [[Veermok (Naboo)|Veermok]].<ref name="Monster">{{GamerCite|2|The Monster}}</ref> Around the same time, [[Rann I-Kanu]], [[Galak]], [[Arani Korden]] and [[Rorworr (Naboo)|Rorworr]] were attacked by a veermok while investigating the presence of a group of [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] based in the jungle near [[Theed/Legends|Theed]].<ref name="SoNFPG">{{Wizards|url=starwars/article.asp?x=rpg_fastPlay_intro|text=The Smugglers of Naboo|int=The Smugglers of Naboo}}</ref>

Veermoks were at one point imported to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Like many other imported species, such as [[Anooba/Legends|anoobas]] and [[saw-toothed grank]]s, they escaped, roamed the [[Coruscant Underworld|lower levels of Coruscant]], and feasted upon garbage and unfortunate life forms.<ref name="Wildlife" />

Prior to the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a [[Veermok Cave|cave]] that was mined by [[Jandosan Mines]] for its ore in the [[Gallo Mountains/Legends|Gallo Mountains]] on Naboo was overtaken by a pack of giant veermoks, causing all mining activities to be stopped.<ref name="SWG:ac">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=herald|a commoner|Naboo}}</ref> The [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Ronin Lightrunner]] later visited the cave during his studies about veermoks.<ref name="SWG:RL" />

During the Galactic Civil War, [[Maulers|Mauler]] [[Beastmaster/Legends|beast masters]] trained veermoks for fighting.<ref name="SWG:MS">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=poi|Mauler Stronghold|Naboo}}</ref> After the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], a race of veermoks smaller in size and living near beaches were discovered on Naboo. As scientists were not able to explain the changes in stature and natural habits, a theory that these beasts were [[Bioengineering/Legends|bioengineered]] and let loose into the wild as emerged. This theory had been rejected by planetary authorities and [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] [[Philosopher/Legends|philosophers]] who simply considered pygmy veermoks as an anomaly.<ref name="Sony" />

Following the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|Destruction of Alderaan]], the [[Alderaanian/Legends|Alderaanian]] brothers [[Heeth Panteer|Heeth]] and [[Raal Panteer]] settled a [[Unidentified moon (Ryloth system)|moon]] in the [[Ryloth system/Legends|Ryloth system]] as a natural reserve. They imported fauna and flora from all around the galaxy to this moon, including veermoks.<ref name="Empire20">[[Empire 20|''Empire'' 20]]</ref>

In the [[New Jedi Order]], [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Jedi initiate]] between the ages of 13 to 14 were part of the [[Clan (Jedi)/Legends|Jedi training clan]] named [[Veermok Clan]] after the Naboo creature.<ref name="Inferno">''[[Legacy of the Force: Inferno]]''</ref>
